boundaries.barrio_lodging.plain: How many places to stay (hotels, inns, guest houses, resorts, vacation properties and other lodging) have their map pin inside the barrio.
boundaries.barrio_lodging.plain_es: Cuántos lugares para hospedarse (hoteles, posadas, casas de huéspedes, complejos turísticos, alquileres vacacionales y otros alojamientos) tienen su marcador dentro del barrio.
boundaries.barrio_lodging.definition: Count of tourism places in the barrio (see boundaries.barrio_assets) in the ACCOMMODATIONS category. The category holds these types: Lodging, Hotels, Vacation Properties, Inns, Guest Houses and Resorts.
boundaries.barrio_lodging.method: build_barrios in landuse.py adds 1 for each counted place whose category is ACCOMMODATIONS.
boundaries.barrio_lodging.how_to_read: Use it to see where lodging listings cluster. It counts listings, not rooms or beds. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the island has 1,831 lodging places: Hotels (1,029), Vacation Properties (426), Lodging (234), Inns (70), Guest Houses (36) and Resorts (36). Barrio values run from 0 to 137 and add up to 1,809.
caveats: It is not an inventory of licensed rooms. Listings in Overture may be incomplete or out of date.

These are listings from Overture Maps, not a count of short-term rentals and not an official room inventory. The type Lodging also holds campgrounds, RV parks and other accommodation that the observatory could not classify more closely.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, barrio totals (1,809) are lower than the island count of lodging places (1,831) because 22 lodging places fall in no barrio.
boundaries.barrio_lodging.source_detail: Overture Maps places, mapped to the observatory's ACCOMMODATIONS category; Census TIGERweb county subdivisions

boundaries.barrio_sfha.plain: How many of the barrio's tourism places sit inside an area the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) maps as high flood risk, the area with a 1% chance of flooding in any year.
boundaries.barrio_sfha.plain_es: Cuántos de los lugares turísticos del barrio están dentro de un área que FEMA (Agencia Federal para el Manejo de Emergencias) marca como de alto riesgo de inundación: el área con 1% de probabilidad de inundarse en cualquier año.
boundaries.barrio_sfha.definition: Count of tourism places in the barrio (see boundaries.barrio_assets) whose pin lies inside a polygon of the Federal Emergency Management Agency's National Flood Hazard Layer with SFHA_TF = T. That is a Special Flood Hazard Area: zones A, AE, AH, AO, A99 and the coastal V zones (VE in the data).
boundaries.barrio_sfha.method: Each place is tested against the flood polygons when places are flagged (point_flags in build.py). Where polygons overlap the Special Flood Hazard Area wins. The barrio adds up the flags.
boundaries.barrio_sfha.how_to_read: A high number means many listed places lie in an area FEMA maps as having a 1% chance of flooding in any year (about 1 in 4 over 30 years). It is not a forecast of when flooding happens, and it says nothing about the building's elevation or insurance. In the 2026-10 snapshot, values run from 0 to 150 and add up to 4,216.
caveats: It describes the mapped hazard at the pin, not the building.
Areas outside the mapped flood zones are not necessarily safe; flood maps may be out of date.
Places in zones where FEMA has not determined the hazard, and places outside the mapped polygons, count as not in a flood hazard area.

In the 2026-10 snapshot, barrio totals (4,216) are lower than the municipality total (4,468) because 325 places fall in no barrio. Almost all of those pins are at or just off the coast, where mapped flood zones are common: 252 of the 325 are in a flood hazard area. The barrio counts therefore leave out 5.6% of flood-zone places (252 of 4,468), against 1.3% of all places (325 of 24,209).
boundaries.barrio_sfha.source_detail: Overture places; FEMA NFHL layer 28, DFIRM_ID LIKE '72%'; Census TIGERweb county subdivisions

view.label: Map, Map layers tab: Barrios (click inside a barrio)

boundaries.barrio_assets.plain: How many tourism places (restaurants, attractions, lodging and visitor services) have their map pin inside the barrio.
boundaries.barrio_assets.plain_es: Cuántos lugares turísticos (restaurantes, atracciones, alojamientos y servicios para visitantes) tienen su marcador dentro del barrio.
boundaries.barrio_assets.definition: Count of listings in places.json with confidence of 0.50 or more and a type other than Places of Worship whose pin lies inside the barrio polygon. The places are gastronomy, attractions, accommodations and visitor services together.
boundaries.barrio_assets.method: See boundaries.barrio_stats. Places come from Overture Maps and carry a confidence score from the source.
boundaries.barrio_assets.how_to_read: A high count means many listed businesses and sites in that barrio. It does not say how many visitors they receive. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 23,884 places are counted in a barrio, and the count runs from 0 (24 barrios) to 1,233 (Santurce, San Juan).
caveats: The file calls this field assets. It counts listed places, not financial or physical assets, and only places the observatory classes as gastronomy, attractions, accommodations or visitor services; other businesses are not counted.
Overture coverage is uneven; barrios with few listings may have businesses that are not in the source.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, listings were last updated between November 2020 and September 2026; some businesses may have closed.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, 325 places (1.3%) fall in no barrio and are not counted here.
Barrios are different sizes. Compare with places per km².
boundaries.barrio_assets.source_detail: Overture Maps Places (in the 2026-10 snapshot, listing update dates run from November 2020 to September 2026); Census TIGERweb county subdivisions

view.label: Map, Map layers tab: Barrios (click inside a barrio)

boundaries.barrio_assets_per_km2.plain: Tourism places in the barrio divided by its area in square kilometers. It shows how crowded a barrio is with listed places, whatever its size.
boundaries.barrio_assets_per_km2.plain_es: Los lugares turísticos del barrio divididos entre su área en kilómetros cuadrados. Muestra qué tan lleno de lugares listados está un barrio, sea cual sea su tamaño.
boundaries.barrio_assets_per_km2.definition: assets divided by km2, using the unrounded area, rounded to 2 decimals.
boundaries.barrio_assets_per_km2.method: build_barrios in landuse.py: round(assets / km2, 2), where km2 is the unrounded polygon area.
boundaries.barrio_assets_per_km2.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot, values run from 0 to 322.19 (the barrio Barceloneta, in Barceloneta: 33 places in about 0.1 km²). The highest values are in small barrios. The top five are Barceloneta, Cabo Rojo, Luquillo, Dorado and Quinto (in Ponce); all but Quinto are barrios-pueblo (town centers) in the Census layer. Compare barrios of similar size.
caveats: Very small barrios can show large values from a handful of places.
The area can include some inland water, which lowers the density slightly.

Do not compare it with places per km² in municipalities.json. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the barrio value uses the observatory's polygon area, which can include inland water, and counts only the 23,884 places inside a barrio. The municipality value uses the 2020 Census land area and counts all 24,209 places.
boundaries.barrio_assets_per_km2.source_detail: Overture Maps places divided by Census-based polygon area

boundaries.barrio_transit.plain: How many of the barrio's tourism places have a mapped bus stop, train station or ferry terminal within 400 m (a quarter mile), measured in a straight line. It counts stops whose timetable has ended and stops that volunteers mapped.
boundaries.barrio_transit.plain_es: Cuántos de los lugares turísticos del barrio tienen una parada de guagua, estación de tren o terminal de lancha del mapa a 400 m (un cuarto de milla) o menos, medidos en línea recta. Cuenta las paradas cuyo horario ya terminó y las que mapearon personas voluntarias.
boundaries.barrio_transit.definition: Count of tourism places in the barrio whose nearest mapped stop of any kind (transit stop, bus stop, bus station, rail station or ferry terminal) is 400 m or less away in a straight line. Stops come from the ATI timetable feed (the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado), municipal timetable feeds and OpenStreetMap bus stops, bus and rail stations and ferry terminals. Taxi stands, charging stations, airports and helipads do not count. The field transit minus acc_cur400 is the number of the barrio's places within 400 m of a mapped stop but of no stop with a current timetable.
boundaries.barrio_transit.method: access.py finds the nearest mapped stop of any kind for each place and sets transit_400m when the distance is 400 m or less (see places.transit_400m). build_barrios in landuse.py adds up the flags of the counted places in each barrio.
boundaries.barrio_transit.how_to_read: A high number means many places are near a mapped stop. It does not say whether buses run often or at useful hours. For places near a stop whose timetable has not ended, see acc_cur400. In the 2026-10 snapshot, values run from 0 to 1,218 and add up to 11,429.
caveats: Distance is a straight line, not the walking route.

Stops from expired timetables and volunteer-mapped stops still count, so real service may be thinner. In the 2026-10 snapshot 131 barrios have a value above 0 but no place near a stop with a current timetable.
A barrio with no stop in the data shows 0, which can mean no data rather than no service.

In the 2026-10 snapshot, barrio totals (11,429) are lower than the island count (11,507) because 78 places near a mapped stop fall in no barrio. The barrio counts are rebuilt only at a full build; the nightly refresh does not update them.
boundaries.barrio_transit.source_detail: Overture places; ATI and municipal GTFS feeds; OpenStreetMap; Census TIGERweb county subdivisions

municipalities.sfha_pct.plain: Out of every 100 counted tourism places in the municipality, this many sit in a high-risk flood area. The US Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) maps that area with a 1% chance of flooding each year.
municipalities.sfha_pct.plain_es: De cada 100 lugares turísticos contados en el municipio, cuántos están en un área de alto riesgo de inundación. FEMA (Agencia Federal para el Manejo de Emergencias) marca esa área con 1% de probabilidad de inundarse cada año.
municipalities.sfha_pct.definition: in_sfha divided by assets, times 100, rounded to one decimal. The build leaves it empty when a municipality has no counted places. In the 2026-10 snapshot, all 78 have a value, the island share is about 18.5% (4,468 of 24,209, from the municipality counts) and the median municipality is 14.2%.
municipalities.sfha_pct.method: round(in_sfha / assets x 100, 1) in build.py. Places of worship and listings below confidence 0.50 are excluded from both numbers.
municipalities.sfha_pct.how_to_read: A high value means many of the municipality's counted places sit in the mapped 1% flood area. This is the share of counted tourism places with a pin in that area. It is not the share of the municipality's land, homes or residents in a flood area. In the 2026-10 snapshot, Salinas (73.7%), Cataño (73.0%), Guayanilla (63.1%), Loíza (54.5%) and Guánica (52.6%) are highest. Florida is 0%. The Municipality tab also ranks municipalities by this share (1 = highest).
caveats: A municipality with few places can swing widely. In the 2026-10 snapshot, Maricao has 36 counted places and 4 in a flood hazard area (11.1%): one more place in the area would raise its share by about 2.4 points, and one more place outside it would lower the share by about 0.3 points. In Salinas (213 places) one place moves the share by about 0.1 to 0.3 points.
It describes the mapped hazard at a point, not the building. It says nothing about elevation, flood-proofing or insurance.
The Municipality tab's 'in flood hazard area' tile is counted live from the places the map shows and follows the filters. The map hover, the shading and the Rankings tab use this stored value.
municipalities.sfha_pct.source_detail: Overture Maps places; FEMA NFHL layer 28, DFIRM_ID LIKE '72%'.

Map, Rankings tab: rank by '% of places in flood hazard area'
3D view: Columns by municipality, '% of places in flood hazard area'
Map, Municipality tab: tile 'in flood hazard area'

municipalities.in_sfha.plain: How many counted tourism places sit inside an area that the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) maps as having a 1% chance of flooding in any year. This is the Special Flood Hazard Area, often called the 100-year floodplain.
municipalities.in_sfha.plain_es: Cuántos lugares turísticos contados están dentro de un área que FEMA (Agencia Federal para el Manejo de Emergencias) marca con 1% de probabilidad de inundarse en cualquier año. Es el Área Especial de Riesgo de Inundación (SFHA), conocida como la zona inundable de 100 años.
municipalities.in_sfha.definition: Number of the counted places (assets) whose pin (the point where Overture places the listing) lies inside a FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer polygon marked as a Special Flood Hazard Area (SFHA_TF = 'T'). Counted places are Overture listings with a confidence score of 0.50 or higher, without places of worship (see 'Which places each municipality count includes'). It is a part of in_flood_zone, which also counts the 0.2% area. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the 78 values add up to 4,468, and the counted places fall in zones A, AE, AO, A99 and VE (AE includes regulatory floodways).
municipalities.in_sfha.method: Point-in-polygon test of each place against the FEMA flood polygons, then a count per municipality of the counted places that tested inside. See 'How flood and protected-area exposure is counted' for the rules on overlaps and ignored zones.
municipalities.in_sfha.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot, Ponce has the most places in a flood hazard area (540), then San Juan (473), Carolina (194) and Cabo Rojo (181). Florida has none: in the FEMA layer the observatory used, one polygon of minimal flood hazard covers all of Florida. Use sfha_pct for the share of a municipality's places.
caveats: It tests the pin only. It says nothing about the building's elevation, floor level, flood-proofing or insurance, or about past flooding.
A 1% annual chance does not mean the area floods once in 100 years. It can flood in any year, and over 30 years the chance is about 26%.

These flags are a screening count from map pins. They are not a flood zone determination for any property: FEMA's metadata names its Flood Insurance Rate Map, database and Flood Insurance Study as the official designation.
It uses FEMA's mapped zones only. Flooding outside them, for example from heavy rain, can still happen.
A pin close to a zone edge can fall on either side, and FEMA revises its maps over time. The 2026-10 snapshot uses the layer downloaded on 1 October 2026.
Large municipalities have more places, so more places in a hazard area. Compare shares, not only counts.
municipalities.in_sfha.source_detail: Overture Maps places; FEMA NFHL layer 28, DFIRM_ID LIKE '72%', fields FLD_ZONE, ZONE_SUBTY, SFHA_TF; 4,894 polygons in the layer downloaded 2026-10-01.

municipalities.in_flood_zone.plain: How many counted tourism places sit in the 1% flood area of the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) or in its lower-risk 0.2% flood area. It is always at least as large as the count for the 1% area alone.
municipalities.in_flood_zone.plain_es: Cuántos lugares turísticos contados están en el área de inundación de 1% de FEMA (Agencia Federal para el Manejo de Emergencias) o en su área de menor riesgo de 0.2%. Siempre es igual o mayor que el conteo del área de 1% sola.
municipalities.in_flood_zone.definition: Number of the counted places whose pin (the point where Overture places the listing) lies inside a FEMA Special Flood Hazard Area (the same test as in_sfha) or inside a FEMA polygon whose subtype is '0.2 PCT ANNUAL CHANCE FLOOD HAZARD' (a shaded zone X). Counted places are Overture listings with a confidence score of 0.50 or higher, without places of worship (see 'Which places each municipality count includes'). So in_flood_zone equals in_sfha plus the places that are in the 0.2% area only. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the 78 values add up to 5,668: 4,468 in a Special Flood Hazard Area and 1,200 in the 0.2% area only.
municipalities.in_flood_zone.method: A place gets a flood zone recorded only when its pin is in a Special Flood Hazard Area or in a polygon whose subtype contains '0.2'. The build counts, per municipality, the counted places with a recorded flood zone. Unshaded zone X (minimal hazard) and zone D leave a place with no flood zone. See 'How flood and protected-area exposure is counted'.
municipalities.in_flood_zone.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot, San Juan has the most (676), and Florida has none. The difference between this field and in_sfha is the number of places in the 0.2% area only. In that snapshot the two counts are equal in 20 municipalities, because no counted place there lies in the 0.2% area alone. The observatory's maps and rankings do not show this field. It is in the data file and the CSV (comma-separated values) download.
caveats: A 0.2% annual chance area is lower risk than the 1% area, but flooding there is still possible.
It tests the pin only, and it uses FEMA's mapped zones only. It does not describe building elevation, insurance or past flooding.
Do not add in_flood_zone to in_sfha: the first already contains the second.
municipalities.in_flood_zone.source_detail: Overture Maps places; FEMA NFHL layer 28, DFIRM_ID LIKE '72%', fields FLD_ZONE, ZONE_SUBTY, SFHA_TF.

places.flood_zone.plain: The flood zone that FEMA (the US Federal Emergency Management Agency) maps at the place's pin. It is shown only when the pin is in a mapped high-risk area (1% annual chance of flooding) or in the 0.2% annual chance area.
places.flood_zone.plain_es: La zona inundable que FEMA (Agencia Federal para el Manejo de Emergencias) marca donde está el marcador del lugar. Solo aparece cuando el marcador está en un área de alto riesgo mapeada (1% de probabilidad anual de inundación) o en el área de 0.2% de probabilidad anual.
places.flood_zone.definition: The FEMA flood zone code of the flood-map polygon that contains the pin. It is published only for places inside a Special Flood Hazard Area (the zones that occur in the 2026-10 snapshot are A, AE, AO, A99 and VE) or inside the shaded 0.2% annual chance zone (zone X with that subtype). In the 2026-10 snapshot, 7,266 of 32,541 places have one (22.3%).
places.flood_zone.method: Point-in-polygon test of the pin against the flood polygons of the National Flood Hazard Layer for Puerto Rico, which FEMA publishes. The observatory skips polygons marked open water or area not included (the 2026-10 download has none). When a pin lies in overlapping polygons, a Special Flood Hazard Area wins over the 0.2% zone. Unshaded zone X (minimal hazard) is not recorded. See 'How flood, protected-area, land-use and transit flags are set'.
places.flood_zone.how_to_read: Zones A, AE, AH, AO, A99 and VE all mean a 1% chance of flooding in any given year, often called the 100-year flood. A 1% annual chance does not mean one flood every 100 years. It is a 1-in-100 chance each year, and it repeats every year. X with the 0.2% subtype is the 500-year area. A place with no flood zone is in neither mapped area. That does not mean it cannot flood.
caveats: This is the mapped hazard at one point. It does not describe the building, its floor height or its insurance.

Missing means the pin is in no mapped Special Flood Hazard Area or 0.2% annual chance area. It may be in unshaded zone X (minimal hazard), in zone D (possible but undetermined flood hazard; 17 places in the 2026-10 snapshot), or outside the area FEMA mapped.
FEMA revises its maps. The 2026-10 snapshot used the layer as downloaded on 1 October 2026.
The descriptions in the codes below are plain-language summaries. The FEMA definitions are the reference.
FEMA's printed Flood Insurance Rate Map and Flood Insurance Study are the official designation. This is a database copy and not a flood determination for any property.
The file does not carry the effective date of the flood map at each place. The observatory downloads only the fields FLD_ZONE, ZONE_SUBTY, SFHA_TF and STATIC_BFE.
The place counts in the table of codes are from the 2026-10 snapshot.

values.A: Special Flood Hazard Area: 1% annual chance of flooding in any year. FEMA has not set flood elevations. 264 places.
values.A99: Special Flood Hazard Area: 1% annual chance of flooding, in an area a federal flood protection system under construction is meant to protect. 89 places.
values.AE: Special Flood Hazard Area: 1% annual chance of flooding in any year. FEMA has set base flood elevations. 3,916 places.
values.AO: Special Flood Hazard Area: 1% annual chance of shallow flooding, usually 1 to 3 feet deep. 567 places.
values.VE: Coastal Special Flood Hazard Area: 1% annual chance of flooding, with extra hazard from storm waves. 805 places.
values.X: Shown here only with the subtype 0.2 PCT ANNUAL CHANCE FLOOD HAZARD: area with a 0.2% annual chance of flooding in any year (the 500-year flood). Outside the Special Flood Hazard Area. 1,625 places.

places.flood_subtype.plain: FEMA (the US Federal Emergency Management Agency) adds a detail to some flood zones. It marks either a floodway, a river channel and nearby land kept clear for floodwater, or the 0.2% annual chance area.
places.flood_subtype.plain_es: FEMA (Agencia Federal para el Manejo de Emergencias) agrega un detalle a algunas zonas inundables. Marca un cauce mayor (floodway), es decir, el cauce de un río y el terreno cercano que se mantienen libres para el agua de las inundaciones, o el área de 0.2% de probabilidad anual.
places.flood_subtype.definition: The FEMA zone subtype of the polygon that contains the pin. It is published only for places that have a flood zone, and in the 2026-10 snapshot only two values occur: FLOODWAY and 0.2 PCT ANNUAL CHANCE FLOOD HAZARD. 2,205 places have one.
places.flood_subtype.method: Copied from the ZONE_SUBTY field of the same flood polygon used for the flood zone. See 'How flood, protected-area, land-use and transit flags are set'.
places.flood_subtype.how_to_read: A floodway is part of the Special Flood Hazard Area. The 0.2% area is outside it. Most places with a flood zone have no subtype.
caveats: Like the flood zone, this is the mapped hazard at one point, not a description of the building.
A missing subtype does not mean the place is outside a floodway when it has no flood zone at all.

The place pop-up shows the zone only. The subtype is in the downloaded file and in the CSV (comma-separated values) download. The Flood zones (FEMA) layer pop-up shows the subtype of each flood polygon.
The place counts in the table of codes, and the zones named there, are from the 2026-10 snapshot.

values.0.2 PCT ANNUAL CHANCE FLOOD HAZARD: The area with a 0.2% annual chance of flooding in any year (the 500-year flood). All of these places are in zone X. 1,625 places.
values.FLOODWAY: Regulatory floodway: the river channel and nearby land that FEMA says must stay clear so the 1% annual chance flood does not rise more than a set height. All of these places are in zone AE. 580 places.

places.sfha.plain: Yes when the pin is inside a FEMA (US Federal Emergency Management Agency) Special Flood Hazard Area, an area with a 1% chance of flooding in any year. The field is missing otherwise.
places.sfha.plain_es: Sí cuando el marcador está dentro de un Área Especial de Riesgo de Inundación (SFHA) de FEMA (Agencia Federal para el Manejo de Emergencias), un área con 1% de probabilidad de inundarse en cualquier año. Si no, el campo no aparece.
places.sfha.definition: A yes flag (true). In the 2026-10 snapshot, it is present for 5,641 of 32,541 places (17.3%) and for 4,468 of 24,209 places on the default basis (18.5%). It is true when the SFHA_TF field of the FEMA flood map is T for the polygon that contains the pin: zones A, AE, AH, AO, A99 and VE (no place in the 2026-10 snapshot lies in AH). Zone X (0.2%) is not a Special Flood Hazard Area.
places.sfha.method: Point-in-polygon test of the pin against the flood polygons (see the flood zone entry). The municipal figures in_sfha and sfha_pct count this flag on the default basis.
places.sfha.how_to_read: On the map, a dark ring around a pin marks a place with this flag, and the pop-up names the zone. A missing flag is not a promise of safety. Default basis means a confidence score of 0.50 or higher and no places of worship.
caveats: This is the mapped hazard at one point, not the risk to the building. It says nothing about elevation, drainage or insurance.
The flag uses the pin. A pin near the edge of a zone can fall on either side.
The place counts in the table of codes are from the 2026-10 snapshot.

values.true: The pin is inside a Special Flood Hazard Area. 5,641 places.
values.(missing): The pin was not found inside a Special Flood Hazard Area. It may be in the 0.2% annual chance area, in unshaded zone X (minimal hazard), in zone D (possible but undetermined flood hazard; 17 places) or outside the area FEMA mapped. The field is left out of the file instead of being written as false.

municipalities.place_to_municipality.plain: A tourism place belongs to the municipality whose boundary contains its map pin (the point where Overture places the listing). The town named in the address does not decide. If the pin is outside every boundary, the place goes to the municipality whose boundary is nearest.
municipalities.place_to_municipality.plain_es: Un lugar turístico pertenece al municipio cuyo límite contiene su marcador en el mapa (el punto donde Overture ubica el listado). El pueblo que aparece en la dirección no decide. Si el marcador está fuera de todos los límites, el lugar se asigna al municipio cuyo límite está más cerca.
municipalities.place_to_municipality.definition: The build tests each listing's pin (the point where Overture places the listing) against the Census Bureau's shoreline-clipped municipality polygons. A pin inside none goes to the municipality whose polygon is nearest (in the 2026-10 snapshot, the one with the nearest centre point). The result is the municipality field of places.json and the basis of every municipality count of tourism places. The full steps are in 'How municipality and barrio are assigned to a place'.
municipalities.place_to_municipality.method: Function make_muni_locator in build.py, applied to every place after de-duplication. The steps, the part the address town plays while duplicates are folded, and the counts of pins outside every polygon are in 'How municipality and barrio are assigned to a place'.
municipalities.place_to_municipality.how_to_read: Counts agree with the polygons the map draws. A place counted for San Juan has its pin inside San Juan's boundary unless it was one of the few pins outside every boundary. The town named in a listing's address does not decide: in the 2026-10 snapshot, 863 of the 32,541 listings (2.7%) have an address that names a different municipality from the one their pin falls in. Counts of places by municipality in the observatory all follow the pin.
caveats: A wrong pin in Overture puts a place in the wrong municipality.

The boundaries are clipped to the shoreline, so pins on piers, marinas and beaches can fall outside. They are then assigned to the nearest polygon. The 2026-10 build still assigned them by nearest centre, which can be a different municipality from the one the pin is next to. In the 2026-10 snapshot, San Juan has the most such counted places (51).

The boundary drawn on the map is simplified by about 20 metres (0.0002 degrees) for display, so a place very near a border can look as if it is on the wrong side. The build used the same Census generalized 500k layer before this display simplification.
municipalities.place_to_municipality.source_detail: Overture Maps place coordinates; Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k boundaries clipped to the shoreline); centre points from the observatory's list in municipalities.py.

view.label: Map, Municipality tab: the places counted for a municipality (the 'Tourism places' counts and tiles)

municipalities.exposure_method.plain: The observatory checks the map point of each counted tourism place against federal flood-zone maps and protected-area maps, then adds up the places that fall inside, for each municipality.
municipalities.exposure_method.plain_es: El observatorio compara el punto en el mapa de cada lugar turístico contado con los mapas federales de zonas inundables y de áreas protegidas, y luego suma los lugares que caen dentro, por municipio.
municipalities.exposure_method.definition: Each counted place's pin (the point where Overture places the listing) is tested against the flood polygons of the US Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) National Flood Hazard Layer and the protected-area polygons of the Protected Areas Database of the United States (PAD-US) of the US Geological Survey (USGS). Counted places are Overture listings with a confidence score of 0.50 or higher, without places of worship. The results are added up for each municipality in four fields: in_sfha (places in a Special Flood Hazard Area, the area with a 1% yearly chance of flooding), in_flood_zone (places in that area or in the 0.2% area), sfha_pct (in_sfha as a percent of counted places) and in_protected (places inside a protected area). The tests are described in 'How flood exposure of a place is flagged' and 'How a place is flagged as inside a protected area'.
municipalities.exposure_method.method: Function point_flags in build.py runs the two point-in-polygon tests for every place. Function municipality_stats in build.py then counts, for each municipality, the counted places with each flag. The rules for overlapping polygons, ignored zones and proclamation boundaries are in the two entries named in the definition.
municipalities.exposure_method.how_to_read: The test says whether the pin falls inside a mapped hazard area in the layers downloaded for the snapshot (1 October 2026 for the 2026-10 snapshot). It does not say how likely a particular building is to flood. Read the zone letters in the 'values' list as FEMA defines them and check FEMA's own zone definitions for the exact wording.
caveats: The test uses the pin only. It says nothing about building elevation, floor level, flood-proofing, insurance or past flooding.

The test used the full-detail polygons downloaded from FEMA and USGS. The published flood.geojson and protected.geojson are simplified by about 5 metres (0.00005 degrees) for display, so repeating the test on the published files can give slightly different results for pins near an edge.

The observatory does not store the effective date of any FEMA map (the build keeps only the zone, subtype, Special Flood Hazard Area flag and base flood elevation of each polygon), so the flags can reflect maps older than the snapshot date.
A place with no flood flag is not shown to be safe. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 15 counted places are in zone D and 9 are outside every FEMA polygon; none of them is counted as exposed.
Only FEMA's mapped zones count. Flooding outside them, for example from heavy rain, can still happen.
Only counted places (confidence 0.50 or higher, no places of worship) enter the municipality figures. Another filter gives other numbers.

values.A: FEMA zone in the 1% flood area (Special Flood Hazard Area), with no base flood elevation given. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 210 counted places.
values.AE: Zone in the 1% flood area with base flood elevations. Includes regulatory floodways. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 3,255 counted places, of which 505 in a floodway.
values.AO: Zone in the 1% flood area for shallow flooding that spreads over the ground. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 490 counted places.
values.AH: Zone in the 1% flood area for shallow ponding. The layer downloaded 2026-10-01 holds one such polygon, and no counted place falls in it.
values.A99: Zone in the 1% flood area that FEMA expects a federal flood-protection system under construction to protect. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 68 counted places.
values.VE: Coastal zone in the 1% flood area with extra hazard from storm waves (zone V is not present in the layer downloaded 2026-10-01). In the 2026-10 snapshot, 732 counted places.
values.X, 0.2 PCT ANNUAL CHANCE FLOOD HAZARD: Shaded zone X: area with a 0.2% yearly chance of flooding. Counted in in_flood_zone only. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 1,309 counted places.
values.X, AREA OF MINIMAL FLOOD HAZARD: Unshaded zone X: minimal flood hazard. Not counted as flood exposure. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 20,491 counted places.
values.D: Possible but undetermined flood hazard: FEMA has not determined the hazard, which is not the same as no hazard. Not counted as flood exposure. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 15 counted places.
values.No FEMA polygon: The pin lies outside every FEMA polygon used in the test. Not counted as flood exposure. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 9 counted places.

municipalities.exposure_method.source_detail: FEMA NFHL layer 28, DFIRM_ID LIKE '72%', fields FLD_ZONE, ZONE_SUBTY, SFHA_TF, 4,894 polygons, downloaded 2026-10-01. USGS PAD-US 4.1, Protection Mechanism Category layer, State_Nm = 'PR', 665 polygons, downloaded 2026-10-01. Zone meanings are FEMA's.

methods.municipality_assignment.plain: A tourism place or a transit stop belongs to the municipality whose boundary contains its map point. If the point is outside every boundary, such as on a pier, the municipality whose boundary is nearest takes it. Census blocks and barrios use their Census county code.
methods.municipality_assignment.plain_es: Un lugar turístico o una parada de transporte colectivo pertenece al municipio cuyo límite contiene su punto en el mapa. Si el punto queda fuera de todos los límites, como en un muelle, se le asigna al municipio cuyo límite está más cerca. Los bloques censales y los barrios usan su código de condado del Censo.
methods.municipality_assignment.definition: The observatory assigns a municipality in four ways, by kind of record. (1) Tourism places and transport features (stops, stations, terminals, airports, taxi stands, electric vehicle (EV) charging points): the full build tests the point against the Census Bureau's shoreline-clipped municipio polygons (a generalized 1:500,000 layer, boundaries as of January 1, 2023); a point inside no polygon takes the municipality whose polygon is nearest (muni_locate.py). The published tourism places still carry the earlier rule, the nearest centre point listed in municipalities.py, until the next full build. (2) Scheduled transit stops after a nightly transit refresh: tested against the published municipios.geojson, a simplified copy of the polygons; a stop outside every polygon takes the municipality whose polygon is nearest, as in the full build. (3) Census blocks: the municipality comes from the county code in the block's ID. (4) Barrios: the municipality comes from the county code in the barrio's GEOID, and a tourism place gets its barrio from a point-in-polygon test against the barrio polygons. Only counted places (confidence 0.50 or higher, no places of worship) get a barrio, and only when their point falls inside a barrio polygon.
methods.municipality_assignment.method: Functions make_muni_locator and nearest_muni in build.py; the refresh in refresh_network.py; network.coverage for blocks; build_barrios in landuse.py. The address town in Overture's records is used only while duplicate listings are folded, so that listings in different towns are not merged.
methods.municipality_assignment.how_to_read: A municipal count agrees with the polygon drawn on the map. A place counted for San Juan has its point inside San Juan's boundary, unless it is one of the few points outside every boundary. The town named in an address does not decide. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 348 of the 32,541 place listings (324 of the 24,209 counted places) lie outside every polygon and took the nearest centre point (the next full build gives them the nearest polygon, which moves 60 listings, 59 of them counted); for all the others the point-in-polygon result is the published municipality. Of the counted places, 23,884 fall inside a barrio polygon and have a barrio.
caveats: A wrong point in the source puts a place in the wrong municipality.

Boundaries are clipped to the shoreline, so points on piers, marinas and beaches can fall outside. They then go to the municipality whose polygon is nearest. Until the 2026-11 fix they went to the nearest centre point, which can be a different municipality from the one the point is next to: it put the Cataño ferry and bus terminals in San Juan. Scheduled stops follow the new rule since that fix, tourism places from the next full build.
The boundary drawn on the map is simplified for display (about 22 metres, 0.0002 degrees), so a place very near a border can look as if it is on the wrong side.

The nightly refresh tests stops against the simplified copy of the boundaries and the full build against the full-detail ones, so a stop within about 22 metres of a border can land in a different municipality in the two. Both give a stop outside every polygon the municipality whose polygon is nearest. Until the 2026-10 access update the nightly refresh left such a stop without a municipality.
methods.municipality_assignment.source_detail: Overture Maps place coordinates; Census Bureau TIGERweb generalized county boundaries (layer 11) and 2020 blocks; transit stops from the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) and municipal General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) feeds and from OpenStreetMap.

municipalities.counting_rules.plain: Three counts describe the tourism listings in a municipality. They differ only in whether places of worship and low-confidence listings are included. The default, assets, leaves out both.
municipalities.counting_rules.plain_es: Tres conteos describen los listados turísticos de un municipio. Solo se diferencian en si incluyen los lugares de culto y los listados de baja confianza. El conteo predeterminado, assets, deja fuera ambos.
municipalities.counting_rules.definition: All counts start from the same list: Overture listings that fell into the observatory's four tourism categories, after de-duplication, without the listings that are not tourism (homes, housing and care services; since 2026-10-18). listings_all counts every one of them (32,541 on the island in the 2026-10 snapshot). assets_all_confidence drops the places of worship (27,509 in that snapshot). assets also drops the listings with an Overture confidence score below 0.50 (24,209 in that snapshot). The other tourism counts in municipalities.json (by_category, in_sfha, in_flood_zone, in_protected, with_website, avg_confidence, sfha_pct and both density ratios) are calculated from the assets places only.
municipalities.counting_rules.method: Steps in build.py. (1) parse_places keeps Overture records whose category maps to one of the observatory's tourism categories and drops the rest. (2) dedup folds duplicate listings: two listings in the same municipality (at this step the town in the address, or the nearest centre point when the address names none) and the same category are merged when their names are alike and they are close together (within 600 m, or 1,000 m when either listing is a beach, park, nature reserve, scenic area, historic site or tourist attraction, with a tighter limit when the names are only partly alike), or when they share a phone number, have partly matching names and lie within 500 m. The record with the highest confidence and the most complete details is kept. Then the listings that are not tourism (homes, housing, care services and numbered homes filed under tourism categories; places_privacy.not_tourism) are left out of every count (HANDOFF decision 47, 2026-10-18). (3) Each place gets a municipality from its pin. (4) Flood and protected-area flags are added. (5) municipality_stats counts. The confidence cutoff is MIN_CONF = 0.50. A place of worship is any listing of the type 'Places of Worship'.
municipalities.counting_rules.how_to_read: Use assets for tourism supply. Use assets_all_confidence to see how much a municipality's count depends on the 0.50 cutoff. Use listings_all only to reconcile with the full list of places in places.json (32,541 rows in the 2026-10 snapshot).
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, 99,323 Overture places lay in the bounding box, 36,206 matched a tourism category, and 1,088 of those were folded into other listings as duplicates; 2,577 more are not tourism and were left out (since 2026-10-18). The largest single group of dropped records, 3,388, has no Overture category at all.

Places of worship are the only type left out by name. All are Attractions. In the 2026-10 snapshot there are 5,032 such listings, of which 4,758 have confidence of 0.50 or higher. Foundation for Puerto Rico's (FPR) keyword rule for this type also matches the word 'religious', so besides churches and other places of worship it holds 1,169 listings that Overture calls religious organizations and 67 religious schools. All 5,032 are left out of assets.
The map's category chips, confidence slider and worship toggle change what the map draws and what the Municipality tab counts live. They never change the stored counts.

Transit access (transit_pct, access_n and the acc_ shares) and the barrio counts use the same counted places. The municipality land-use place figures (places_urban_pct, places_on_protected_land and places_on_protected_land_pct) differ: they use all listings in listings_all, including places of worship and listings below 0.50. Each is documented in its own entry.
municipalities.counting_rules.source_detail: Overture Maps places theme, release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 2026-10-01.

places.land_group.plain: The broad group of the land-use plan class at the place's pin: urban, urbanizable, rustic (ordinary rural), protected, water or road.
places.land_group.plain_es: El grupo amplio de la clase del plan de uso de terrenos donde está el marcador del lugar: urbano, urbanizable, rústico (rústico común), protegido, agua o vías.
places.land_group.definition: One of six groups that the observatory derives from the plan class (land_use). In the 2026-10 snapshot, it is present for the same 32,369 places as land_use.
places.land_group.method: Set from the plan class: SU is urban; SURP and SURNP are urbanizable; SRC is rustic; any class starting with SREP is protected; AGUA is water; VIAL is road.
places.land_group.how_to_read: Use it for quick counts, for example places on urban land. Protected here means rural land under special protection in the plan. It is a different thing from a protected area in PAD-US (Protected Areas Database of the United States).
caveats: The group name protected can mislead. The plan's special protection and the PAD-US protected-area database are two separate sources, so a place can be in one and not the other.
Water and road mean the pin sits on a mapped water or road polygon.
The Junta de Planificación states no data license, and its website footer reads Todos los derechos reservados (all rights reserved). Check the Junta's terms before you reuse this field.
The place counts in the table of codes are from the 2026-10 snapshot.

values.rustic: Ordinary rural land: class SRC. 2,795 places.
values.protected: Specially protected rural land: every class that starts with SREP. 2,151 places.
values.urbanizable: Urbanizable land, reserved for urban growth: classes SURP (programmed) and SURNP (not programmed). 58 places.

Map, Municipality tab: a municipality's places, with a CSV download that has a land_group column (example: San Juan)

places.land_use.plain: The class of Puerto Rico's 2015 land-use plan (Plan de Uso de Terrenos, PUT) at the place's pin, such as urban land or ordinary rural land.
places.land_use.plain_es: La clase del Plan de Uso de Terrenos (PUT) de Puerto Rico de 2015 donde está el marcador del lugar, como suelo urbano o suelo rústico común.
places.land_use.definition: The class code (CLASIPUT) of the Plan de Uso de Terrenos (PUT) polygon that contains the pin. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 32,369 of 32,541 places have one. The other 172 fall outside every plan polygon; the largest groups are in San Juan (25), Fajardo (19), Culebra (18) and Cabo Rojo (13), and all 4 places on Mona Island are among them.
places.land_use.method: Point-in-polygon test of the pin against the plan's polygons at full detail. If polygons overlap, the first one found is used. See 'How flood, protected-area, land-use and transit flags are set'.
places.land_use.how_to_read: The plan classes land by what the plan intends or allows: urban, urbanizable (future growth), rural or specially protected rural. It is a planning class. It is not the actual use of the building, and it is not zoning (calificación).
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, 5,858 places (18.0%) sit in road (VIAL) polygons, because the plan maps roads as their own polygons. Such a place is usually next to the road.
The plan dates from 2015. Land can have changed class since then.
Zoning districts (calificación) are not in the observatory's data: the Junta de Planificación's online service did not return them when the 2026-10 snapshot was built.
The Junta de Planificación states no data license, and its website footer reads Todos los derechos reservados (all rights reserved). Check the Junta's terms before you reuse this field.
The place counts in the table of codes are from the 2026-10 snapshot.

municipalities.places_on_protected_land_.plain: Out of every 100 place listings in the municipality that fall inside the 2015 land use plan, how many sit on specially protected rural land.
municipalities.places_on_protected_land_.plain_es: De cada 100 registros de lugares del municipio que caen dentro del Plan de Uso de Terrenos 2015, cuántos están en suelo rústico especialmente protegido.
municipalities.places_on_protected_land_.definition: places_on_protected_land divided by the municipality's listings whose point falls inside any plan polygon (urban, urbanizable, ordinary rural, protected, water or road), times 100, rounded to one decimal. Listings that fall in no polygon are not counted in the denominator.
municipalities.places_on_protected_land_.method: Listings in protected polygons divided by listings in any plan polygon, per municipality, times 100. Water and road polygons count in the denominator. See land.put_statistics.
municipalities.places_on_protected_land_.how_to_read: A high value means many of the municipality's listings stand on protected rural land; a low value means few do. It is a share of listings, not of land area (see protected_land_pct). In the 2026-10 snapshot the value ranges from 0.0% to 44.7% (Maricao); Adjuntas 34.9%, San Juan 0.3%. Of the island's 32,541 listings in that snapshot, 172 fall in no polygon.
caveats: The Housing page profile shows this figure under the label "Tourism places on protected rural land". The figure counts all place listings (32,541 on the island in the 2026-10 snapshot), including places of worship and listings below confidence 0.50, so it is not a count of tourism places alone (24,209 in that snapshot, the number counted in assets). See municipalities.counting_rules.
The denominator includes listings on road and water polygons, so shares are lower than a share of places on land only.
A plan designation from 2015: it shows how the Junta de Planificación classified the land, not today's land cover or what stands on it.
The Junta de Planificación states no data license, and its site footer reads "Todos los derechos reservados". Check its terms before reusing the plan or figures computed from it.

municipalities.places_on_protected_land.plain: How many place listings in the municipality sit on land the 2015 land use plan classes as specially protected rural land. It counts all listings, not only tourism places.
municipalities.places_on_protected_land.plain_es: Cuántos registros de lugares del municipio están en terreno que el Plan de Uso de Terrenos 2015 clasifica como suelo rústico especialmente protegido. Cuenta todos los registros de lugares, no solo los lugares turísticos.
municipalities.places_on_protected_land.definition: Number of place listings whose point falls inside a plan polygon of class SREP (Suelo Rústico Especialmente Protegido) or one of its subtypes, among the listings that the point-in-polygon test assigns to the municipality. Listings are the Overture Maps places that the observatory keeps after classification and de-duplication: they include places of worship and listings below confidence 0.50.
municipalities.places_on_protected_land.method: landuse.py tests each listing's point against the plan polygons and takes the first polygon that contains it. A listing in a protected group polygon is counted for the municipality where its point falls. See land.put_statistics.
municipalities.places_on_protected_land.how_to_read: It shows how many listed places stand on land the plan protects. A listing on protected land is not necessarily a problem: nature reserves, parks and scenic areas are listed places too. In the 2026-10 snapshot the island has 2,151 such listings, in 77 of the 78 municipalities.
caveats: The Housing page profile shows this figure under the label "Tourism places on protected rural land". The figure counts all place listings (32,541 on the island in the 2026-10 snapshot), including places of worship and listings below confidence 0.50, so it is not a count of tourism places alone (24,209 in that snapshot, the number counted in assets). See municipalities.counting_rules.
Not the same as in_protected, which counts tourism places inside protected areas of the US Geological Survey (USGS) Protected Areas Database (PAD-US).
A plan designation from 2015: it shows how the Junta de Planificación classified the land, not today's land cover or what stands on it.
A point near a polygon edge can fall in either polygon; the first polygon found is used.
The Junta de Planificación states no data license, and its site footer reads "Todos los derechos reservados". Check its terms before reusing the plan or figures computed from it.

municipalities.places_urban_pct.plain: Out of every 100 place listings in the municipality that fall inside the 2015 land use plan, how many sit on land the plan classes as urban.
municipalities.places_urban_pct.plain_es: De cada 100 registros de lugares del municipio que caen dentro del Plan de Uso de Terrenos 2015, cuántos están en terreno que el plan clasifica como urbano.
municipalities.places_urban_pct.definition: Listings whose point falls inside a plan polygon of class SU (Suelo Urbano), divided by the municipality's listings whose point falls inside any plan polygon (urban, urbanizable, ordinary rural, protected, water or road), times 100, rounded to one decimal. Listings in no polygon are not counted.
municipalities.places_urban_pct.method: Listings in urban polygons divided by listings in any plan polygon, per municipality, times 100. Road and water polygons count in the denominator and never in the numerator. See land.put_statistics.
municipalities.places_urban_pct.how_to_read: A high value means most listings stand on urban land. In the 2026-10 snapshot the value ranges from 29.8% (Maricao) to 81.6% (Guaynabo), and 66.2% of listings island-wide (21,418 of 32,369) stand on urban land. Listings on a street polygon (5,858 of those 32,369, 18.1%) are not counted as urban, even in a town centre. The value therefore understates the share of listings in built-up areas.
caveats: This count uses every place listing in the municipality (32,541 on the island in the 2026-10 snapshot), including places of worship and listings below confidence 0.50, not only the tourism places counted in assets. See municipalities.counting_rules.
Not the same as urban_pct, which is a share of land area.
A plan designation from 2015: it shows how the Junta de Planificación classified the land, not today's land cover or what stands on it.
The Junta de Planificación states no data license, and its site footer reads "Todos los derechos reservados". Check its terms before reusing the plan or figures computed from it.

municipalities.in_protected.plain: How many counted tourism places have their map pin (the point where Overture places them) inside a protected area in PAD-US, the US Geological Survey's Protected Areas Database of the United States. Many of these areas are local parks.
municipalities.in_protected.plain_es: Cuántos lugares turísticos contados tienen su marcador en el mapa (el punto donde Overture los ubica) dentro de un área protegida de PAD-US, la base de datos de áreas protegidas de Estados Unidos del USGS (Servicio Geológico de Estados Unidos). Muchas de estas áreas son parques locales.
municipalities.in_protected.definition: Number of the counted places (assets) whose pin lies inside a polygon of the US Geological Survey's (USGS) Protected Areas Database of the United States (PAD-US) in Puerto Rico, other than a proclamation boundary (designation type PROC). Counted places are Overture listings with a confidence score of 0.50 or higher, without places of worship (see 'Which places each municipality count includes'). A place that is inside several polygons counts once. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the 78 values add up to 869, and five municipalities have none: Añasco, Las Marías, Maricao, Maunabo and Moca.
municipalities.in_protected.method: Point-in-polygon test of each place against the PAD-US polygons, then a count per municipality of the counted places that tested inside. See 'How flood and protected-area exposure is counted'.
municipalities.in_protected.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot, San Juan has the most (134), then Río Grande (50), Guánica (38) and Ponce (36). Of the 869 counted places inside a protected area in that snapshot, the strictest status of the area is 4 for 509 places, 2 for 252, 1 for 62 and 3 for 46. This is the GAP code of the US Geological Survey's Gap Analysis Project: 1 = managed for biodiversity, natural disturbance allowed; 2 = managed for biodiversity, disturbance held back; 3 = managed for several uses, such as mining or logging; 4 = no known requirement to protect biodiversity. The map words these codes differently (it labels GAP 1 'strict nature reserve'); see 'Protection level, GAP status (GAP_Sts)'.
caveats: 'Protected' refers to the land's conservation or management status. It does not mean the place is protected from flooding, storms or other hazards.

'Protected' here means any area listed in PAD-US. The layer downloaded for the 2026-10 snapshot includes local parks (411 of its 665 polygons), marine protected areas, conservation easements, wildlife refuges and military lands. It does not mean the place is in a nature reserve.

In the 2026-10 snapshot, one PAD-US record named 'Unknown Local Park' covers 117 of the 869 places (13%), 12 of them in San Juan. That record is a set of 534 separate local-park areas (managing agency unknown), not one park. Counts for municipalities with many local-park places partly reflect it.
Being inside the polygon does not say whether the public can enter. Access differs by area, and the map pop-up for an area shows it.
It is not the same as the share of land in 'Suelo Rústico Especialmente Protegido' in the Junta de Planificación's 2015 land-use plan, which is a different source and a different field.
It tests the pin only and counts places, not hectares.
municipalities.in_protected.source_detail: Overture Maps places; USGS PAD-US 4.1, Protection Mechanism Category layer, State_Nm = 'PR'; 665 polygons in the layer downloaded 2026-10-01.

places.protected_area.plain: The name of the protected area that contains the place's pin. The names come from PAD-US, the US Geological Survey's Protected Areas Database. In the 2026-10 snapshot, about 3% of places have one.
places.protected_area.plain_es: El nombre del área protegida que contiene el marcador del lugar. Los nombres vienen de PAD-US, la base de datos de áreas protegidas del USGS (Servicio Geológico de Estados Unidos). En el corte de datos de 2026-10, alrededor del 3% de los lugares tiene una.
places.protected_area.definition: The unit name (Unit_Nm) of the PAD-US area that contains the pin. If several areas contain it, the one with the strictest GAP (Gap Analysis Project) status is named. Proclamation boundaries, which outline whole islands or refuges, do not count. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 1,013 places have one (3.1%), 869 of them on the default basis, and 307 different names occur.
places.protected_area.method: Point-in-polygon test of the pin against the PAD-US polygons of Puerto Rico. Of the areas that contain the pin, the one with the lowest GAP status number is used. See 'How flood, protected-area, land-use and transit flags are set'.
places.protected_area.how_to_read: PAD-US lists land that is public or held for conservation or recreation. Being inside one does not mean the place is in a nature reserve: PAD-US also lists local parks, plazas and military land. Read the protection level (GAP status) next to it. Default basis means a confidence score of 0.50 or higher and no places of worship.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, 140 places show the name 'Unknown Local Park'. PAD-US records those local parks without a name.
Only one area is named even when the pin lies in several.
This is a database match, not a legal or zoning finding. The land-use plan class is a separate field.

places.protected_gap.plain: The protection level, from 1 (strictest) to 4 (no known mandate to protect nature), of the area named in the protected area field. The scale is the GAP status of the USGS (US Geological Survey) Gap Analysis Project.
places.protected_gap.plain_es: El nivel de protección, de 1 (el más estricto) a 4 (sin mandato conocido de proteger la naturaleza), del área que nombra el campo de área protegida. La escala es el estatus GAP del Gap Analysis Project del USGS (Servicio Geológico de Estados Unidos).
places.protected_gap.definition: The USGS GAP status code of the PAD-US (Protected Areas Database of the United States) area named in protected_area, written as the digit 1, 2, 3 or 4. It is published together with protected_area: in the 2026-10 snapshot, 1,013 places have both.
places.protected_gap.method: Copied from the GAP_Sts field of the PAD-US area chosen for protected_area, which is the area with the lowest GAP number among those containing the pin.
places.protected_gap.how_to_read: GAP 1 and 2 areas are managed for biodiversity. GAP 4 means no known mandate to protect biodiversity. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 608 of the 1,013 places with a value are GAP 4, so most places with a protected area are on land with no known biodiversity mandate. The place pop-up shows the area name only. The GAP status is in the downloaded file, in the CSV (comma-separated values) download and in the Protected areas layer pop-up.
caveats: GAP status describes protection of biodiversity. It does not describe public access. PAD-US has a separate access field that the observatory does not publish for each place.
The descriptions in the codes below paraphrase USGS. The PAD-US data dictionary is the reference. "Strict nature reserve" is the map's label for code 1, not PAD-US wording.
The place counts in the table of codes are from the 2026-10 snapshot.

values.1: GAP status 1: managed for biodiversity. Natural disturbance, such as fire or flooding, is allowed to happen or is imitated by management. The pop-up of the Protected areas layer labels it "strict nature reserve", but PAD-US does not use that term. 67 places.
values.2: GAP status 2: managed for biodiversity, but natural disturbance is suppressed, for example fires are put out. The Protected areas layer pop-up calls it managed for biodiversity. 285 places.
values.3: GAP status 3: managed for multiple uses. Extractive uses such as mining or logging, or off-highway vehicle use, may be allowed. The Protected areas layer pop-up calls it multiple use, some extraction. 53 places.
values.4: GAP status 4: no known requirement to protect biodiversity. The land is recorded in PAD-US (for example local parks, plazas, a national historic site and military land) but is not protected for biodiversity. The Protected areas layer pop-up calls it no known biodiversity mandate. 608 places.

municipalities.listings_all.plain: Every tourism listing in the municipality after de-duplication, including places of worship and low-confidence listings. It is the largest of the three place counts.
municipalities.listings_all.plain_es: Todos los listados turísticos del municipio después de quitar los duplicados, incluidos los lugares de culto y los listados de baja confianza. Es el mayor de los tres conteos de lugares.
municipalities.listings_all.definition: Number of de-duplicated listings attached to the municipality in any of the observatory's four tourism categories, including places of worship (a type of Attractions) and listings of every confidence score. It equals the number of rows of places.json for that municipality. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the 78 values add up to 32,541: 27,509 other places plus 5,032 places of worship.
municipalities.listings_all.method: Count of all places attached to the municipality after classification, de-duplication and municipality assignment, with no further filter.
municipalities.listings_all.how_to_read: Use it to reconcile with the full list of places in places.json. In the 2026-10 snapshot, San Juan has 4,597 listings and Maricao 47. For tourism supply use assets.
caveats: It includes churches and other places of worship, which are mapped as landmarks but are mostly not tourism supply, and records Overture rates below 0.50.

The type Places of Worship comes from the observatory's keyword rule, which also matches the word 'religious'. In the 2026-10 snapshot it holds 5,032 listings: besides churches and other places of worship, 1,169 listings that Overture calls religious organizations and 67 religious schools.
It does not include every Overture place. Records with no tourism category (for example salons, clinics or gas stations) were dropped before counting.
The map does not display this field; it is in the data file and in the CSV (comma-separated values) download.
municipalities.listings_all.source_detail: Overture Maps places theme, release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 2026-10-01; municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k boundaries clipped to the shoreline).

municipalities.avg_confidence.plain: The average of Overture's own confidence scores for the municipality's counted tourism places. A score is a number from 0 to 1, and a higher number means Overture is more sure the listing is a real place.
municipalities.avg_confidence.plain_es: El promedio de las puntuaciones de confianza que el propio Overture da a los lugares turísticos contados del municipio. La puntuación es un número de 0 a 1; mientras más alto, más seguro está Overture de que el listado es un lugar real.
municipalities.avg_confidence.definition: Mean of the Overture confidence scores of the places counted in assets, rounded to three decimals. Counted places all score 0.50 or higher, so the mean cannot fall below 0.50. All 78 municipalities have a value.
municipalities.avg_confidence.method: Sum of the confidence of each counted place divided by the number of counted places, per municipality, rounded to three decimals in build.py. The observatory does not compute the confidence itself.
municipalities.avg_confidence.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot, the averages run from 0.780 (Peñuelas) to 0.850 (San Juan). The range is narrow because only scores of 0.50 or higher are averaged. Treat it as a rough data-quality signal, not as an accuracy rate.
caveats: The score is produced by Overture, and the observatory has not checked it against the real places.
It is calculated after the 0.50 cutoff, so it cannot show how many weaker listings were left out. See assets_all_confidence for that.
The map does not display this field; it is in the data file and in the CSV (comma-separated values) download.
municipalities.avg_confidence.source_detail: Overture Maps places theme, release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 2026-10-01; field confidence of each place.

municipalities.assets.plain: How many tourism places the municipality has: attractions, food and drink, lodging and visitor services. Places of worship are left out. A place counts only if Overture Maps, an open map-data project, gives it a confidence score of 0.50 or higher.
municipalities.assets.plain_es: Cuántos lugares turísticos tiene el municipio: atracciones, lugares de comida y bebida, alojamientos y servicios para visitantes. Quedan fuera los lugares de culto. Un lugar cuenta solo si Overture Maps, un proyecto abierto de datos de mapas, le da una puntuación de confianza de 0.50 o más.
municipalities.assets.definition: Number of de-duplicated Overture Maps listings in the municipality that (1) fall into one of the observatory's four tourism categories (Attractions, Gastronomy, Accommodations, Visitor Services), (2) are not places of worship and (3) have an Overture confidence score of 0.50 or higher. This is the default basis for the tourism statistics in the observatory. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the 78 values add up to 24,209.
municipalities.assets.method: In the 2026-10 snapshot, Overture had 99,323 places inside Puerto Rico's bounding box. The rules of Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR) matched 36,206 of them to a tourism category and dropped the rest. Duplicates were folded (1,088), leaving 35,118 listings, and the 2,577 that are not tourism (homes, housing and care services filed under tourism categories) were left out, leaving 32,541 (since 2026-10-18, HANDOFF decision 47). Each listing was attached to a municipality by its pin, the point where Overture places the listing (see 'How a tourism place is assigned to a municipality'). The build then counts, per municipality, the listings that are not places of worship and have confidence of at least 0.50 (MIN_CONF in build.py). See 'Which places each municipality count includes'.
municipalities.assets.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot, San Juan has the most counted places (3,424) and Maricao the fewest (36). Large municipalities have more, so compare places per 1,000 residents or per km² before ranking places against each other. The Municipality tab's first tile, 'tourism places (current filters)', is counted live from the places the map shows, so it changes when you change the category chips or the confidence slider; this stored value does not. In municipalities.json and in the CSV (comma-separated values) download, this count is the column 'assets'. A snapshot is one build of the observatory. The 2026-10 snapshot (label 'Snapshot 2026-10') was generated on 2 October 2026 (UTC) from Overture release 2026-09-23.1.
caveats: It counts listings, not businesses, rooms, beds or visitors.

In the 2026-10 snapshot, nearly two thirds of the counted places (17,170 of 24,209) are food and drink places such as restaurants, bars and cafés, which serve residents as well as visitors. 'Tourism places' is FPR's label for the four categories. It does not count only places that visitors use.
A low count can mean that Overture lists fewer places there. The count is not an inventory and does not match official hotel, room or business counts, which use other records and definitions.

Overture builds its listings from several sources and some are wrong, closed or missing. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 23,618 of the 24,209 counted places come from Meta, 250 from Foursquare, 238 from Microsoft and 103 from AllThePlaces. The confidence score is Overture's, and FPR has not checked it on the ground.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, the sources last updated the counted listings between November 2020 and September 2026, so the count does not describe one date.

Overture records whose category is outside the four groups are not counted at all. Among the most common dropped categories are beauty salons, grocery stores, professional services, auto repair, doctors' offices, gas stations, spas and schools.
One business can appear twice if its records differ more than the de-duplication rules allow, and two real places can be folded into one.

In the 2026-10 snapshot, about 1% of the counted places (324 of 24,209) have a pin outside every municipal boundary polygon, such as pins at the shoreline. That build counted them for the municipality with the nearest centre point; the next full build counts them for the municipality whose boundary is nearest.
Do not read two snapshots as growth or decline. Each snapshot uses a new Overture release and a new run of FPR's matching and de-duplication rules.

municipalities.by_category.plain: Four counts for each municipality: its attractions, its food and drink places (gastronomy), its lodging (accommodations) and its visitor services. Together they add up to the municipality's tourism places.
municipalities.by_category.plain_es: Cuatro conteos para cada municipio: sus atracciones, sus lugares de comida y bebida (gastronomía), sus alojamientos y sus servicios para visitantes. Juntos suman los lugares turísticos del municipio.
municipalities.by_category.definition: An object with four keys, ATTRACTIONS, GASTRONOMY, ACCOMMODATIONS and VISITOR_SERVICES. Each holds the number of the counted places (assets) in that category. Counted places are Overture listings with a confidence score of 0.50 or higher, without places of worship (see 'Which places each municipality count includes'). All four keys are present for all 78 municipalities (the value is 0 when there is none), and the four numbers add up to assets.
municipalities.by_category.method: The observatory assigns each Overture listing to a category and a type by matching Overture's category names against keyword rules in build.py (RULES). The build then counts the places counted in assets by category. Places of worship, which are Attractions, are excluded.
municipalities.by_category.how_to_read: Use it to compare the mix of supply: in the 2026-10 snapshot, 2,421 of San Juan's 3,424 places are Gastronomy, while 51 of Culebra's 136 are Accommodations. In the CSV (comma-separated values) download the object is split into four columns: by_category_ATTRACTIONS, by_category_GASTRONOMY, by_category_ACCOMMODATIONS and by_category_VISITOR_SERVICES. The Analysis tab maps the four counts as separate layers.
caveats: The category comes from the observatory's keyword rules on Overture's category names, not from the business. A place can be put in a category that a visitor would not choose.
Accommodation listings are not rooms or beds. A hotel with 400 rooms is one place.
The Municipality tab's 'By category' bars are counted live from the places the map shows. They do not read this object and change with the filters.

values.ATTRACTIONS: Attractions: 4,591 places island-wide in the 2026-10 snapshot. Types present: historic sites, parks, beaches, tourist attractions, cultural attractions (such as galleries, theatres and cinemas), scenic areas, museums and nature reserves. Places of worship are not counted here.
values.GASTRONOMY: Gastronomy, meaning food and drink: 17,170 places island-wide in the 2026-10 snapshot. Types present: restaurants, bars, cafés, bakeries, nightlife and food experiences.
values.ACCOMMODATIONS: Accommodations: 1,831 places island-wide in the 2026-10 snapshot. Types present: lodging (the general type, including campgrounds), hotels, vacation properties, inns, guest houses and resorts.
values.VISITOR_SERVICES: Visitor services: 617 places island-wide in the 2026-10 snapshot. Types present: transportation (such as airports, bus stations and taxi services), adventure operators, tour operators, cultural experience providers, marinas and visitor centers.

municipalities.with_website.plain: How many of the counted tourism places list a website in their Overture record.
municipalities.with_website.plain_es: Cuántos de los lugares turísticos contados tienen un sitio web en su registro de Overture.
municipalities.with_website.definition: Number of the counted places (assets) whose Overture record lists at least one website. Counted places are Overture listings with a confidence score of 0.50 or higher, without places of worship (see 'Which places each municipality count includes'). The build keeps the first website Overture gives and counts only whether one is present. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the 78 values add up to 7,210, which is 30% of the 24,209 counted places.
municipalities.with_website.method: Count of places in assets with a non-empty website field. The website addresses themselves are published in places.json, except that the build removes a few that contain an email address.
municipalities.with_website.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot, San Juan has the most places with a website (1,597) and Florida the fewest (7). As a share of counted places, the range in that snapshot is from about 8% in Maunabo to 47% in San Juan (worked out from the municipal values). Use it as a rough sign of how visible a place is online, not as a measure of quality.
caveats: The address is not checked. It may be out of date or lead to a page that no longer exists.

A website can be a social page or a booking listing. Before 2026-10-18, among the 7,440 website addresses then published for counted places (26,579 then counted), 527 contained instagram.com or facebook.com and 293 contained airbnb.com (42 more used Airbnb's abnb.me short link). Website addresses are no longer published.

In the 2026-10 snapshot a recount of has_website in places.json gives the same value for every municipality. Before 2026-10-18 the recount was 1 lower in Ponce, because one website was counted before the build removed an address holding an email address; that listing is no longer counted.
On the Municipality tab, the 'with a website' tile is counted live from the places the map shows and follows the filters.

municipalities.assets_all_confidence.plain: Tourism places counted at every confidence score, still without places of worship. It is a larger count that includes the listings Overture is less sure about.
municipalities.assets_all_confidence.plain_es: Los lugares turísticos contados con cualquier puntuación de confianza, todavía sin los lugares de culto. Es un conteo mayor que incluye los listados de los que Overture está menos seguro.
municipalities.assets_all_confidence.definition: Number of de-duplicated listings in the municipality that fall into one of the observatory's four tourism categories and are not places of worship, whatever their Overture confidence score (0 to 1). It is never lower than assets. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the 78 values add up to 27,509, against 24,209 for assets.
municipalities.assets_all_confidence.method: Same listings and municipality assignment as assets, without the confidence cutoff of 0.50. Places of worship are still left out.
municipalities.assets_all_confidence.how_to_read: The gap between this field and assets is the number of listings with confidence below 0.50. In the 2026-10 snapshot it is 3,300 on the whole island, 639 in San Juan and 2 in Maricao. A big gap means the municipality's count depends more on where the cutoff is set.
caveats: Listings below 0.50 are the ones Overture rates as less likely to be real places. The observatory does not use this count for its tourism supply figures.

The map does not display this field; it is in the data file and in the CSV (comma-separated values) download. The map's confidence slider recounts places in the browser and never changes this stored value.

municipalities.assets_per_1000_residents.plain: How many counted tourism places there are for every 1,000 people who live in the municipality.
municipalities.assets_per_1000_residents.plain_es: Cuántos lugares turísticos contados hay por cada 1,000 personas que viven en el municipio.
municipalities.assets_per_1000_residents.definition: assets divided by population_2020, times 1,000, rounded to two decimals. For comparison, in the 2026-10 snapshot the whole island has about 7.37 (24,209 places for 3,285,874 residents, worked out from the municipal values, not stored in the file).
municipalities.assets_per_1000_residents.method: round(assets / population_2020 x 1000, 2) in build.py. It uses the default places basis (confidence 0.50 or higher, no places of worship) and the 2020 Census population.
municipalities.assets_per_1000_residents.how_to_read: A higher number means more tourism places for each resident. In the 2026-10 snapshot, Culebra (75.89), Rincón (29.10) and Vieques (28.73) are highest. Trujillo Alto (2.73) and Toa Alta (2.92) are lowest. The ratio does not measure visitors or demand. In the 2026-10 snapshot, nearly two thirds of the counted places are food and drink places, which serve residents too.
caveats: It divides by residents on census day 2020. Visitors, seasonal residents and people who work there but live elsewhere are not in the denominator.
Small populations make the ratio jump. Culebra had 1,792 residents in the 2020 Census.
The Municipality tab shows this stored value. It does not change with the map's filters, unlike the tiles for the number of places, flood share, protected places and websites.

The Analysis tab's 'Per 1,000 residents' option for tourism layers divides by the Census Bureau's latest population estimate in the observatory (July 1, 2025), not the 2020 count, so its values differ from this field (in the 2026-10 snapshot, San Juan is 10.38 there and 10.00 here). Do not mix the two.

Places are from 2026 and residents from 2020. Puerto Rico's July 2025 estimate (3,184,835) is 3.1% below the 2020 count (3,285,874), so island-wide this ratio would be about 3% higher with 2025 residents. Municipalities differ.

municipalities.assets_per_km2.plain: How many counted tourism places there are on each square kilometre of the municipality's land.
municipalities.assets_per_km2.plain_es: Cuántos lugares turísticos contados hay en cada kilómetro cuadrado de tierra del municipio.
municipalities.assets_per_km2.definition: assets divided by land_km2, rounded to two decimals. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the whole island has about 2.7 (24,209 places on 8,868.5 km², worked out from the municipal values, not stored in the file).
municipalities.assets_per_km2.method: round(assets / land_km2, 2) in build.py, using the default places basis and the 2020 Census land area.
municipalities.assets_per_km2.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot, San Juan is densest (27.59 places per km²), then Rincón (11.95) and Cataño (11.84). Maricao is least dense (0.38). Places cluster in town centres, so the average over a whole municipality hides how crowded the centre is. The Barrios layer on the map shows places per km² for smaller areas, on a different basis, so do not compare the two values (see 'Tourism places per km² (barrio)').
caveats: It uses land area only. Water inside the boundary does not lower the density.
Mayagüez's land area includes Isla de Mona and Monito. In the 2026-10 snapshot, only 3 of its 589 counted places sit there, which lowers its density.
The Municipality tab shows this stored value. It does not change with the map's filters.
