places.category.accommodations.plain: Places to stay: hotels, resorts, inns, guest houses, vacation rentals and other lodging.
places.category.accommodations.plain_es: Lugares para hospedarse: hoteles, complejos turísticos, posadas, casas de huéspedes, alquileres vacacionales y otros alojamientos.
places.category.accommodations.definition: One of the observatory's four tourism categories (code ACCOMMODATIONS, gold pins on the map). It holds 6 types (places in the file, 2026-10 snapshot): Hotels (1,165), Vacation Properties (586), Lodging (301), Inns (88), Resorts (45), Guest Houses (40). In the 2026-10 snapshot the category has 2,225 places in the file and 1,831 on the default basis.
places.category.accommodations.method: Every listing in Overture's lodging group maps here (2,225 places in the 2026-10 snapshot). Its type comes from the first rule that fits, or Lodging when none fits. Listings outside that group never become Accommodations.
places.category.accommodations.how_to_read: Compare the four categories to see the mix of supply, and open the types for detail. Counts are places (one per listing kept after duplicates are folded), not visitors, rooms or size. Default basis means a confidence score of 0.50 or higher and no places of worship.
caveats: Counts are listings, not rooms or beds. A large hotel and a small guest house count once each.
The observatory does not use an official lodging register, and lodging that no source lists is missing. See the Vacation Properties type for what it does not count.

places.category.attractions.plain: Places to see or visit: beaches, parks, museums, historic sites, scenery, cultural venues and similar places. It also holds places of worship, which the observatory does not count by default.
places.category.attractions.plain_es: Lugares para ver o visitar: playas, parques, museos, sitios históricos, paisajes, lugares culturales y similares. También incluye los lugares de culto, que el observatorio no cuenta por defecto.
places.category.attractions.definition: One of the observatory's four tourism categories (code ATTRACTIONS, blue pins on the map). It holds 9 types (places in the file, 2026-10 snapshot): Places of Worship (5,032), Historic Sites (1,098), Tourist Attractions (972), Parks (969), Beaches (840), Cultural Attractions (555), Scenic Areas (398), Museums (173), Nature Reserves (60). In the 2026-10 snapshot the category has 10,097 places in the file, 5,065 without places of worship, and 4,591 on the default basis.
places.category.attractions.method: Listings in Overture's cultural_and_historic, arts_and_entertainment and geographic_entities groups map here (6,123, 1,508 and 1,443 listings in the 2026-10 snapshot). Beaches, parks, nature reserves, scenic areas, historic sites, museums and places of worship are also accepted from other Overture groups (sports_and_recreation gives 947 places in that snapshot, mostly parks), because those types may stand alone. The other 76 places come from education (67, religious schools), shopping (7), services_and_business (1) and travel_and_transportation (1). Overture's group is not published in places.json; these counts come from the Overture records used for the 2026-10 snapshot.
places.category.attractions.how_to_read: Compare the four categories to see the mix of supply, and open the types for detail. Places of worship are not counted by default. Counts are places (one per listing kept after duplicates are folded), not visitors, rooms or size. Default basis means a confidence score of 0.50 or higher and no places of worship.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, places of worship (5,032 listings) are in this category but are left out of counts by default.
Historic Sites and Tourist Attractions are broad types. Read their entries before you draw conclusions.

places.category.gastronomy.plain: Places to eat and drink: restaurants, bars, cafes, bakeries, lounges, distilleries and wineries.
places.category.gastronomy.plain_es: Lugares para comer y beber: restaurantes, barras, cafés, panaderías, lounges, destilerías y vinícolas.
places.category.gastronomy.definition: One of the observatory's four tourism categories (code GASTRONOMY, green pins on the map). It holds 6 types (places in the file, 2026-10 snapshot): Restaurants (11,471), Bars (3,876), Cafes (2,848), Bakeries (1,100), Nightlife (106), Food Experiences (28). In the 2026-10 snapshot the category has 19,429 places in the file and 17,170 on the default basis.
places.category.gastronomy.method: Every listing in Overture's food_and_drink group maps here (19,429 places in the 2026-10 snapshot). Its type comes from the first rule that fits, or Restaurants when none fits. Listings outside that group never become Gastronomy.
places.category.gastronomy.how_to_read: Compare the four categories to see the mix of supply, and open the types for detail. Counts are places (one per listing kept after duplicates are folded), not visitors, rooms or size. Default basis means a confidence score of 0.50 or higher and no places of worship.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, Gastronomy is the largest category: 60% of all places in the file and 71% of those on the default basis.
Food Markets is a defined type with no places in the 2026-10 snapshot. Grocery stores (1,478) and farmers markets (61) were left out in that snapshot.

places.category.visitor_services.plain: Businesses that serve visitors: tour operators, marinas and boat businesses, adventure operators, transportation, visitor centers and cultural experience providers (in the 2026-10 snapshot, all of these providers are dance studios). The map writes this category as Visitor Services.
places.category.visitor_services.plain_es: Negocios que atienden a visitantes: operadores turísticos, marinas y negocios de botes, operadores de aventura, transporte, centros de visitantes y proveedores de experiencias culturales (en el corte de datos de 2026-10, todos estos proveedores son estudios de baile). El mapa muestra esta categoría como Servicios para visitantes.
places.category.visitor_services.definition: One of the observatory's four tourism categories (code VISITOR_SERVICES, red pins on the map). It holds 6 types (places in the file, 2026-10 snapshot): Transportation (204), Tour Operators (192), Adventure Operators (172), Cultural Experience Providers (121), Marinas (96), Visitor Centers (5). In the 2026-10 snapshot the category has 790 places in the file and 617 on the default basis.
places.category.visitor_services.method: Overture has no matching group, so a listing is included only when a Visitor services rule fits its category name. In the 2026-10 snapshot the places come from Overture's travel_and_transportation (445), sports_and_recreation (264), shopping (63), services_and_business (15) and lifestyle_services (3) groups.
places.category.visitor_services.how_to_read: Compare the four categories to see the mix of supply, and open the types for detail. Counts are places (one per listing kept after duplicates are folded), not visitors, rooms or size. Default basis means a confidence score of 0.50 or higher and no places of worship.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, this is the smallest category (790 places in the file, 617 on the default basis). Visitor services that fit no rule are left out.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, car rental offices (174 listings) and other rental businesses are left out. See the classification entry.
Some types hold shops and offices, not only operators, for example surf stores, boat dealers and ferry company offices.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, the Cultural Experience Providers type holds only dance studios. It is 101 of the 617 places of this category on the default basis.

places.overture_category.plain: The category Overture gave the place, such as restaurant, beach or hotel. The observatory keeps it so you can see how each place was classified.
places.overture_category.plain_es: La categoría que Overture le dio al lugar, como restaurant, beach o hotel. El observatorio la conserva para que se pueda ver cómo se clasificó cada lugar.
places.overture_category.definition: Overture's primary category for the listing: lowercase words joined by underscores. 265 different values occur in the 2026-10 snapshot (268 before the listings that are not tourism were left out on 2026-10-18). The observatory uses it, with the parent groups above it in Overture's category tree, to set the category and type.
places.overture_category.method: Copied from the Overture record (taxonomy.primary, or basic_category when the primary is missing). The map pop-up shows it with the underscores replaced by spaces.
places.overture_category.how_to_read: Use it to check or redo the classification: find the code below, then the rule words in the type's entry. The same Overture category can land in a different type when its parent group differs; in the 2026-10 snapshot every code maps to one type.
caveats: The category names and their meaning are Overture's. Overture can rename or add categories between releases.
Some records carry only one of Overture's broad group names (arts_and_entertainment, geographic_entities, food_and_drink, lodging) instead of a specific category.
The place counts in this entry, including those in the table of codes, are from the 2026-10 snapshot.

A few codes sit under an unexpected type because of the text rules. See the notes on trailer_dealer, airport_lounge, marina, the religious codes and the food shops (candy_store, chocolatier, delicatessen).

places.type.plain: The more specific kind of place, such as Beaches, Restaurants or Hotels. The 2026-10 snapshot has 27 types under the four categories.
places.type.plain_es: El tipo de lugar más específico, como Playas, Restaurantes u Hoteles. El corte de datos de 2026-10 tiene 27 tipos en las cuatro categorías.
places.type.definition: One of the 27 type names that occur in the 2026-10 snapshot, set by the observatory from the place's Overture category. Each type belongs to one category. Two more type names appear in the observatory's rules or on the map legend, but no place carries them in that snapshot: Food Markets (Gastronomy) and Landmarks (Attractions).
places.type.method: Ordered text rules, applied to the Overture category and its parent groups. The first rule that matches decides the type, and then the place's Overture group can override it. See 'How Overture categories become tourism categories'.
places.type.how_to_read: Types appear in map pop-ups, in a municipality's list of top types and in search. A type is a rule-based label, so read the type's own entry to see what it includes and leaves out. Default basis means a confidence score of 0.50 or higher and no places of worship.
caveats: Several types are broader or narrower than their names. For example Historic Sites includes many residential buildings, Marinas holds boat businesses, and, in the 2026-10 snapshot, Cultural Experience Providers holds only dance studios.
The place counts in this entry, including those in the table of codes, are from the 2026-10 snapshot.

places.category.plain: The tourism group a place belongs to: Attractions, Gastronomy, Accommodations or Visitor services.
places.category.plain_es: El grupo turístico al que pertenece un lugar: Atracciones, Gastronomía, Alojamientos o Servicios para visitantes.
places.category.definition: One of four codes set by the observatory from the place's Overture category: ATTRACTIONS, GASTRONOMY, ACCOMMODATIONS or VISITOR_SERVICES. The map writes the last one as Visitor Services. Places of worship are filed under ATTRACTIONS.
places.category.method: Ordered text rules read the Overture category and its parent groups. See 'How Overture categories become tourism categories'.
places.category.how_to_read: Use it to filter places and to compare the mix of supply. Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR) set the four groups. They are not an official or industry classification. Each place has one category and one type. Default basis means a confidence score of 0.50 or higher and no places of worship.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, places of worship (5,032 listings) carry the code ATTRACTIONS but are left out of counts by default.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, Gastronomy is the largest group by a wide margin: 19,429 of 32,541 places in the file (60%). Keep that in mind when you compare groups.
The place counts in the table of codes are from the 2026-10 snapshot.

places.not_published.plain: The observatory does not publish the phone, email, social-media links, street address, website, postcode, brand name or source license label of an Overture record, and it removes a telephone number written into a name.
places.not_published.plain_es: El observatorio no publica el teléfono, el correo electrónico, los enlaces a redes sociales, la dirección, el sitio web, el código postal, el nombre de marca ni la etiqueta de licencia de la fuente de un registro de Overture, y quita el número de teléfono escrito en un nombre.
places.not_published.definition: Eight fields of Overture's records are read by the build but never written to places.json: phone, email, socials (social-media links), address (the street address), website, postcode, brand (the brand name) and source_license (the license label of the contributing source). Only whether a website is listed is kept (has_website). The field region is not written either: the map works it out from the municipality. A place the map does not draw also loses its name, Overture ID, coordinates, nearest stop and update date (see Counted but not drawn).
places.not_published.method: The build removes these eight fields when it writes each place (places_privacy.py). Phone numbers are used only to match duplicate listings. The counts of phone, website, email, address and social links decide which duplicate is kept. Postcode, brand and license label are read and dropped without use. The build also leaves out any field that is empty or false, and removes a telephone number or an email address written into a name. Until 2026-10-18 the street address and the website were published; the owner rule of that date is never to publish business contact details or any personal data.
places.not_published.how_to_read: Contact details of individual businesses can identify people, so the observatory leaves these fields out. In the 2026-10 snapshot, among the 32,541 published places, the Overture record holds a phone number for 24,077 (74%), an email address for 12,711 (39%), social-media links for 32,104 (99%), a street address for 27,235 (84%), a website for 9,416 (29%), a postcode for 26,760 (82%) and a brand name for 1,963 (6%). Those fields are not in the observatory's data. Names are copied as the source wrote them, apart from a telephone number or an email address (see the caveats).
caveats: None of the eight fields is written to the published file. Phone numbers are used only to match duplicate listings. Phone, website, email, address and social links are counted to decide which duplicate is kept.

Names are free text. A telephone number or an email address written into a name is removed (4 names in the 2026-10 snapshot); names are not otherwise scrubbed. The street addresses and websites published until 2026-10-18 held telephone numbers (at least 6 addresses, and 28 websites pointed to WhatsApp) and social-media pages that can belong to individuals; they are no longer published, but copies made before that date can still hold them.
CSV (comma-separated values) downloads from the map hold only the published fields.
The source license label is not published for each place. The labels per source are listed in the codes of the contributing data source entry.

places.dedup.plain: When several listings look like the same place, the observatory keeps the one with the highest confidence and counts the others in the duplicates field. In the 2026-10 snapshot, this folded 1,088 listings.
places.dedup.plain_es: Cuando varios listados parecen ser el mismo lugar, el observatorio se queda con el de mayor confianza y cuenta los demás en el campo de duplicados. En el corte de datos de 2026-10, esto unió 1,088 listados.
places.dedup.definition: Two listings count as the same place when they share a municipality (taken from the address town, see step 1) and a category, sit close together, and have alike names (or the same phone number and somewhat alike names). Matches chain: if A matches B and B matches C, all three become one place.
places.dedup.method: The build groups listings by municipality and category, compares nearby pairs, and joins pairs whose names are alike. It keeps the listing with the highest confidence and counts the others in the duplicates field. The steps are listed below.
places.dedup.how_to_read: A place with a duplicates value above 0 stands for several listings. The map pop-up shows the count. Rankings and counts use the kept listing only.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, most groups are small: 574 of the 691 places with folded listings have exactly one.

A few groups are large. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the two largest groups (43 and 36 folded listings) are built on neighborhood names (Condado and Isla Verde) and mix beaches, parks, condominiums and other places that share the name. The kept listing is only one of them.
Folded listings can have different types (for example a beach and a park), and the type of the kept listing is the one published. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 290 groups mix types.
Listings in different municipalities or different categories are never compared, so some real duplicates remain.
The step runs before the confidence cut and before the municipality is set from the pin, so a low-confidence listing can be folded into a higher one, and the group uses the address town.

Folding can remove places from the default count. It is done within a category, not a type, and the highest-confidence listing is kept. Places of worship share the Attractions category, so in the 2026-10 snapshot 74 listings of other types (67 with confidence 0.50 or higher) were folded into a kept place of worship, which is not counted by default. The other way round, 19 places of worship were folded into a kept listing of another type. These figures come from re-running the folding step on the Overture release used for that snapshot, for the places in the file.

values.Step 1: Group listings: Same municipality and same category. The municipality here is the address town when it names one of the 78 municipalities (accents and capital letters ignored). Otherwise it is the nearest municipality center. In the 2026-10 snapshot, among the 32,541 published places, 325 have no address town and 590 have a town text that is not a municipality name.
values.Step 2: Compare pairs: Pairs within 1,000 m if either listing is a Beach, Park, Nature Reserve, Scenic Area, Historic Site or Tourist Attraction; within 600 m for all other types.
values.Step 3: Same place when: The name similarity is 0.95 or more; or it is 0.80 or more and the listings are within 600 m (those natural types) or 150 m (all other types); or the listings share the same phone number, the similarity is 0.50 or more and they are within 500 m.
values.Step 4: Chain the matches: Matching pairs are joined into groups. If A matches B and B matches C, all three are one place.
values.Step 5: Keep one: The listing with the highest confidence is kept. Ties go to the listing with more contact details on file (website, phone, email, address), then to the one with more social links. The duplicates field is the group size minus 1.
values.Name similarity: Names are compared as sets of words. Accents and capital letters are ignored, words shorter than 3 letters are dropped, and common words are dropped (for example the, de, playa, hotel, restaurante, church and the names of the 78 municipalities). The two names must share a word of 4 letters or more. The score is the shared words divided by all words, or, when the shorter name has two or more words (or both names are short), the shared words divided by the shorter name's words times 0.9, whichever is higher.

places.point_tests.plain: Flood zone, protected area, land-use class, barrio and municipality are set by checking which map polygon contains the place's pin. Transit access is the distance to the nearest mapped stop and to the nearest stop with a current timetable.
places.point_tests.plain_es: La zona inundable, el área protegida, la clase de uso de terrenos, el barrio y el municipio se asignan buscando qué polígono del mapa contiene el marcador del lugar. El acceso al transporte colectivo es la distancia a la parada más cercana del mapa y a la parada más cercana con horario vigente.
places.point_tests.definition: Each flag is a spatial test of the pin (latitude and longitude) against another dataset. Nothing is read from the place's name, address or category.
places.point_tests.method: The build checks whether the pin lies inside a polygon of each of these datasets: FEMA (Federal Emergency Management Agency) flood polygons (flood zone, subtype and Special Flood Hazard Area flag), PAD-US (Protected Areas Database of the United States) polygons (protected area and GAP (Gap Analysis Project) status), the land-use plan polygons (land use and group), Census barrio polygons (barrio) and Census municipality polygons (municipality). A pin exactly on a polygon's edge does not count as inside. Where polygons overlap, a Special Flood Hazard Area wins over the 0.2% zone for flood; the lowest GAP number wins for protected areas, and proclamation boundaries are ignored; the first polygon found is used for land use and barrio. The tests use the polygons at the detail the sources give them, not the simplified copies drawn on the map. Transit is different: access.py finds the nearest mapped stop of any kind and stores its distance, its name and the 400 m flag in places.json (see places.transit_m), and finds the nearest stop with a current timetable, which it stores in place_access.json (see place_access.ts_m).
places.point_tests.how_to_read: Read each flag as 'the dataset says this about the spot where the pin is'. It is not a finding about the building or the lot.
caveats: The result depends on how accurate the pin is and on how detailed and how current each polygon dataset is. A pin near an edge can fall on either side.
Only one value is kept per field, even when several polygons overlap the pin.
The Census boundaries are generalized by the Census Bureau, so pins close to the coast or to a boundary can fall on the other side of the true line.

places.municipality_assignment.plain: The municipality comes from where the map pin sits, tested against Census boundaries. The barrio comes from the same kind of test against Census barrio boundaries.
places.municipality_assignment.plain_es: El municipio sale de dónde está el marcador del mapa, comparado con los límites del Censo. El barrio sale de la misma prueba con los límites de barrios del Censo.
places.municipality_assignment.definition: The municipality and the barrio are set from the pin, not from the address text. The address town is used only while duplicate listings are folded.
places.municipality_assignment.method: Step 1 (used only to fold duplicates): the municipality is the address town when it matches one of the 78 municipality names (ignoring accents and capital letters). Otherwise it is the nearest municipality center. Step 2 (published): after folding, each pin is tested against the Census Bureau's shoreline-clipped municipality polygons. The polygon that contains the pin gives the municipality. Step 3: a pin that is inside no polygon (offshore, or at a gap in the shoreline) takes the municipality whose polygon is nearest (in the 2026-10 snapshot, the nearest municipality center). Step 4: for places counted by default only (confidence 0.50 or higher, no places of worship), the pin is tested against the Census barrio polygons. The first polygon that contains it gives the barrio.
places.municipality_assignment.how_to_read: The published municipality is where the pin is, so counts agree with the boundaries drawn on the map. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 863 places have an address town that names another municipality. Default basis means a confidence score of 0.50 or higher and no places of worship.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, 348 places fall in no municipality polygon and took the nearest center. For example, one beach pin on Mona Island falls outside every polygon and took Rincón, while the other three listings on the island are in Mayagüez. The next full build gives such a pin the nearest polygon instead, which puts that beach in Mayagüez too.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, 325 places on the default basis have no barrio, and places of worship and places below the confidence cut never get one.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, the barrio layer has 901 polygons and 694 different names, so a barrio name alone can point to several municipalities.

places.classification.plain: The observatory reads each Overture category and files the place under one of four tourism categories and one type within it (27 types occur in the 2026-10 snapshot). Places that fit none of them are left out, and so are listings that fit a category but are not tourism: homes, housing and care services (since 2026-10-18).
places.classification.plain_es: El observatorio lee cada categoría de Overture y clasifica el lugar en una de cuatro categorías turísticas y en un tipo dentro de ella (en el corte de datos de 2026-10 aparecen 27 tipos). Los lugares que no caben en ninguna quedan fuera, y también los listados que caben en una categoría pero no son turismo: viviendas, complejos de viviendas y servicios de cuido (desde el 2026-10-18).
places.classification.definition: A set of 28 ordered text rules plus a mapping of Overture's top-level groups, both set by the observatory's build script (the tourism taxonomy of Foundation for Puerto Rico). Overture sorts its categories in a tree, and the top level is called a group here (for example food_and_drink). The rules look for words inside Overture's category names, so a match is by text, not by an official code list.
places.classification.method: The observatory tests each listing's Overture category name against 28 ordered text rules, and then the listing's Overture group can override the result. The five steps and the 28 rules are listed below.
places.classification.how_to_read: Read the rules as a ladder: the first match wins, and then the Overture group can override it. When a result looks odd, find the place's Overture category in the Overture category entry, then the rule words in the type's entry.
caveats: The rules match words inside longer words. For example the word trail also matches trailer dealers (6 places in Scenic Areas in the 2026-10 snapshot).

Rule order changes results. Amusement parks and water parks are filed as Parks, bar-and-grill restaurants as Bars, and beach resorts as Lodging. Rental businesses outside the lodging group are not kept, because the word rental matches a Vacation Properties rule before the Transportation or Marinas rule. So the keywords car_rental, bike_rental and scooter_rental in rule 27 never decide a result.
The word plaza in rule 9 does not keep a listing by itself. In the 2026-10 snapshot, public plazas (114) were left out because Overture does not file them under an attractions group.

In the 2026-10 snapshot, 63,117 of 99,323 Overture places are left out (63.5%), among them 3,388 with no category. After duplicates are folded, 2,577 more listings that fit a category are left out because they are not tourism (homes, housing estates, condominiums and care services; see Counted but not drawn). The most common left-out categories are beauty salon (3,167), grocery store (1,478), professional service (1,419), automotive repair (1,419), doctors office (1,280), auto dealer (1,279), gas station (1,250), spa (1,189). Some visitor-related categories are also left out: travel service (295), car rental service (174), travel and transportation with no finer category (146), public plazas (114), farmers markets (61), souvenir stores (53), boat rental and training (23), flea markets (22), travel companies (19), train stations (18), airlines (18), jet skis rental (14), golf courses (13), all-terrain vehicle (ATV) rental tours (9), motorcycle rental service (8) and bike rental (7). Visitor services counts do not include these businesses.

Food Markets is a defined type with no places in the 2026-10 snapshot. Gastronomy is accepted only for listings in Overture's food_and_drink group, and grocery stores and farmers markets sit in Overture's shopping group.
Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR) set this grouping. It is not an official or industry classification.
The counts in this entry are from the 2026-10 snapshot.

values.Step 1: Take the category name: Take Overture's primary category for the listing, or its basic category when there is no primary. A listing with neither is left out.
values.Step 2: Test the rules: Test that category name against the 28 rules in order: Attractions rules first, then Gastronomy, Accommodations and Visitor services. The first rule that matches gives a category and a type. If no rule matches the name, test the full category path (the group and parent names joined) the same way.
values.Step 3: Find the Overture group: Find the listing's Overture group: the first of lodging, food_and_drink, cultural_and_historic, arts_and_entertainment or geographic_entities in its path (the rules also recognize the older names accommodation, eat_and_drink and attractions_and_activities). Lodging maps to Accommodations, food_and_drink to Gastronomy and the other three to Attractions.
values.Step 4: Let the group decide: If the listing has such a group, keep it. When the rule's category equals the group's category, the rule's type is used. Otherwise the group's category is used with its default type: Lodging, Restaurants or Tourist Attractions.
values.Step 5: Listings with no group: If the listing has no such group, keep it only when a rule puts it in Visitor services, or in Beaches, Nature Reserves, Scenic Areas, Historic Sites, Museums, Parks or Places of Worship. Everything else is left out.
values.Rule 1: Places of Worship: Attractions. Applies when the Overture category name contains place_of_worship, church, cathedral, chapel, synagogue, mosque, temple or religious.
values.Rule 2: Beaches: Attractions. Applies when the Overture category name starts with beach.
values.Rule 3: Parks: Attractions. Applies when the Overture category name is exactly park, ends with _park, starts with park_, or contains playground, national_park or state_park.
values.Rule 4: Nature Reserves: Attractions. Applies when the Overture category name contains nature, forest, wildlife, reserve or botanical.
values.Rule 5: Museums: Attractions. Applies when the Overture category name contains museum.
values.Rule 6: Historic Sites: Attractions. Applies when the Overture category name contains historic, monument, fort, castle or ruin.
values.Rule 7: Cultural Attractions: Attractions. Applies when the Overture category name contains art_gallery, theater, theatre, performing_arts, cultural_center, cinema or movie_theater.
values.Rule 8: Scenic Areas: Attractions. Applies when the Overture category name contains scenic, lookout, viewpoint, waterfall, cave, lake, river, island, mountain, hiking_trail or trail.
values.Rule 9: Tourist Attractions: Attractions. Applies when the Overture category name contains tourist, attraction, amusement, zoo, aquarium, water_park, theme_park, observatory, plaza or landmark.
values.Rule 10: Bakeries: Gastronomy. Applies when the Overture category name contains bakery, pastry, patisserie or donut.
values.Rule 11: Cafes: Gastronomy. Applies when the Overture category name contains cafe, coffee, tea_room, ice_cream, dessert, juice_bar or bubble_tea.
values.Rule 12: Nightlife: Gastronomy. Applies when the Overture category name contains night_club, nightclub, karaoke, lounge, dance_club or live_music.
values.Rule 13: Bars: Gastronomy. Applies when the Overture category name contains the word bar on its own, ends with _bar, starts with bar_, ends with pub, or contains brewery, brewpub, beer_garden, cocktail, sports_bar or wine_bar.
values.Rule 14: Food Markets: Gastronomy. Applies when the Overture category name contains farmers_market, food_market, public_market or grocery, or ends with market.
values.Rule 15: Food Experiences: Gastronomy. Applies when the Overture category name contains winery, distillery, coffee_roaster, food_tour or cooking.
values.Rule 16: Restaurants: Gastronomy. Applies when the Overture category name contains restaurant, food_truck, food_stand, diner, pizzeria, steakhouse, seafood, fast_food, cafeteria, eatery, taqueria, bistro, kiosk or chinchorro.
values.Rule 17: Resorts: Accommodations. Applies when the Overture category name contains resort.
values.Rule 18: Inns: Accommodations. Applies when the Overture category name contains the word inn on its own or bed_and_breakfast.
values.Rule 19: Guest Houses: Accommodations. Applies when the Overture category name contains guest_house, guesthouse, hostel or boarding.
values.Rule 20: Vacation Properties: Accommodations. Applies when the Overture category name contains vacation, villa, cottage, cabin, holiday, rental, apartment_hotel or condo.
values.Rule 21: Hotels: Accommodations. Applies when the Overture category name contains hotel or motel.
values.Rule 22: Lodging: Accommodations. Applies when the Overture category name contains lodging, accommodation, campground, camping or rv_park.
values.Rule 23: Tour Operators: Visitor services. Applies when the Overture category name contains tour, travel_agen, excursion or sightseeing.
values.Rule 24: Visitor Centers: Visitor services. Applies when the Overture category name contains visitor, tourist_information or information_center.
values.Rule 25: Marinas: Visitor services. Applies when the Overture category name contains marina, boat, yacht, harbor, harbour, dock or ferry.
values.Rule 26: Adventure Operators: Visitor services. Applies when the Overture category name contains surf, dive, scuba, snorkel, kayak, zipline, zip_line, rafting, horse, adventure, paddle, sailing, fishing_charter or climbing.
values.Rule 27: Transportation: Visitor services. Applies when the Overture category name contains car_rental, airport, taxi, bus_station, transit, shuttle, limo, bike_rental or scooter_rental.
values.Rule 28: Cultural Experience Providers: Visitor services. Applies when the Overture category name contains cooking_class, art_class, dance_studio, workshop or artisan.

places.pipeline.plain: The observatory takes the places that Overture Maps lists in Puerto Rico and keeps those that fit four tourism categories. It folds duplicates, adds location and hazard flags, and does not copy the phone, email or social-media fields.
places.pipeline.plain_es: El observatorio toma los lugares que Overture Maps lista en Puerto Rico y se queda con los que caben en cuatro categorías turísticas. Une los duplicados, agrega indicadores de ubicación y de riesgo, y no copia los campos de teléfono, correo electrónico ni redes sociales.
places.pipeline.definition: places.json is a list of 32,541 places built from 99,323 Overture records (release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 1 October 2026). It is rebuilt with each snapshot of the observatory (Snapshot 2026-10 here). The file is a JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) list in UTF-8 text with one object for each place and up to 23 fields per place (26 field names occur in the file). It is not GeoJSON: the position is in the separate fields lat and lng.
places.pipeline.method: Step 1: download every Overture place inside the box west -67.97, south 17.85, east -65.20, north 18.57 (all of Puerto Rico, including Mona, Culebra and Vieques) as GeoJSON points (99,323 records in the 2026-10 snapshot). Step 2: classify each record (see the classification entry): in the 2026-10 snapshot, 36,206 fit one of the four categories, and 63,117 are left out. Step 3: fold duplicates (see the duplicates entry): in the 2026-10 snapshot, 1,088 listings are folded into others, which leaves 35,118 listings. Then leave out the listings that are not tourism (homes, housing and care services; see Counted but not drawn): 2,577 in the 2026-10 snapshot, which leaves 32,541 places (since 2026-10-18). Step 4: set the municipality from the pin position. Step 5: test each pin against the FEMA (Federal Emergency Management Agency) flood zones, the PAD-US (Protected Areas Database of the United States) protected areas, the 2015 land-use plan, the transit stops and the barrio boundaries. Step 6: remove the phone, email, social-media, postcode, brand and license fields (see the unpublished fields entry), and write places.json.
places.pipeline.how_to_read: The file is a snapshot of one Overture release. Places that opened, closed or moved after that release are not in it.
caveats: Coverage depends on what Overture's sources list. A place that no source lists is missing, and a place that has closed can still be listed. The observatory does not check places on the ground.

Licenses: Overture's place records carry the license of each contributing source. In the 2026-10 snapshot the labels are CDLA-Permissive-2.0 (Meta and Microsoft records), Apache-2.0 (Foursquare) and CC0-1.0 (AllThePlaces). Read Overture's terms and each source's terms before you reuse or redistribute the records.
The map credits Overture Maps Foundation contributors for place data.

Counts from two snapshots are not comparable as a time series. A new Overture release can add or drop listings from its sources without any business opening or closing, and the observatory does not track openings and closures.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, coverage follows Meta's: 98.2% of the places (31,945 of 32,541) list Meta as the source, so the mix of categories mostly reflects what Meta lists.

places.missing_values.plain: A field that is empty for a place is left out of the file instead of being written as blank or false. So a missing flood zone, protected area or barrio means no value was found, not that the value is zero.
places.missing_values.plain_es: Un campo vacío para un lugar se omite del archivo en vez de escribirse en blanco o como falso. Así que, si falta la zona inundable, el área protegida o el barrio, significa que no se encontró un valor, no que el valor sea cero.
places.missing_values.definition: The observatory does not write a field when its value is missing, false, an empty text or an empty list. That is why the yes flags (sfha and transit_400m) appear only as true, and why optional fields appear on some places and not on others.
places.missing_values.method: The build removes every field whose value is missing, false, an empty text or an empty list, when it writes each place. Numbers, including 0, are kept.
places.missing_values.how_to_read: A missing value is not a measured zero and is not a promise of safety. Read the notes below for each field. In a spreadsheet, an empty cell means the same as a missing field.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot every place has category, type, overture_category, municipality, confidence, source, duplicates and transit_m, and every place the map draws also has oid, name, lat, lng, nearest_stop and updated. The build would leave out name, source or updated for a record that has none.

values.sfha: Missing means the pin was not found inside a Special Flood Hazard Area. Present only as true.
values.transit_400m: Missing means the nearest mapped stop of any kind is more than 400 m away. Present only as true.
values.flood_zone: Missing means the pin is in no mapped Special Flood Hazard Area or 0.2% annual chance area. It may be in unshaded zone X (minimal hazard), in zone D (possible but undetermined flood hazard; 17 places in the 2026-10 snapshot), or outside the area FEMA mapped.
values.flood_subtype: Missing means the place has no flood zone, or its zone has no subtype.
values.protected_area: Missing means the pin is in no PAD-US area (proclamation boundaries do not count).
values.barrio: Missing means the place is not counted by default (worship or below the confidence cut), or its pin is in no barrio polygon.
values.land_use: Missing means the pin is in no land-use plan polygon (in the 2026-10 snapshot, 173 places; the largest groups are in San Juan, Fajardo, Culebra and Cabo Rojo, and all 4 places on Mona Island are among them).
values.has_website: Missing means no source gave a website, or the value held an email address. The web address itself is never published.
values.withheld: Missing means the map draws the place. Present on the places counted but not drawn, which also have no oid, name, lat, lng, nearest_stop or updated.
values.hub_400m: Present only as true, and only on a place the map does not draw.
values.duplicates: Never missing. A place with no folded listings shows 0.
values.transit_m: Never missing. A place at a stop shows 0.
values.ts_m, ts_calls and ts_we (place_access.j: Never missing: the file holds one value for each place, in the order of places.json. ts_calls 0 means no stop with a current timetable within 400 m. ts_we 0 means no stop with a current timetable within 400 m, or no Saturday or Sunday service in the published timetable. ts_m is 99,999 at most.

places.counting_basis.plain: Unless you change the filter, the observatory counts a place only when Overture's confidence score is 0.50 or higher and it is not a place of worship. In the 2026-10 snapshot, that gives 24,209 tourism places.
places.counting_basis.plain_es: Si no se cambia el filtro, el observatorio cuenta un lugar solo cuando la puntuación de confianza de Overture es de 0.50 o más y no es un lugar de culto. En el corte de datos de 2026-10, eso da 24,209 lugares turísticos.
places.counting_basis.definition: The default basis is: confidence of 0.50 or higher, and a type other than Places of Worship. In the 2026-10 snapshot, of the 32,541 places in the file, 5,032 are places of worship and 3,300 more score below 0.50, which leaves 24,209. In this entry a listing is one record about a place in Overture's data (name, location, category, source), and a pin is the point on the map where a place's coordinates sit. After duplicates are folded, the observatory keeps one listing for each place.
places.counting_basis.method: The observatory's build sets the minimum confidence to 0.50. The place counts and shares in municipalities.json (assets, by_category, in_sfha, in_flood_zone, in_protected, with_website, avg_confidence, sfha_pct, places_near_transit, transit_pct, access_n, the acc_ shares and the per-resident and per-km2 rates) and every count in barrios.geojson use that basis. Three exceptions: assets_all_confidence and listings_all, which are meant to show other bases, and places_on_protected_land, places_on_protected_land_pct and places_urban_pct, which count every listing in the file that has a land-use class (32,369 of 32,541 in the 2026-10 snapshot), including places of worship and places below 0.50. meta.json records the cut as min_confidence. The 2D map starts at the same value: the Minimum confidence slider runs from 0 to 1 in steps of 0.05, and the Include places of worship box starts off. The 3D view always uses 0.50 and hides places of worship. A place that scores exactly 0.50 is counted.
places.counting_basis.how_to_read: Use the slider when you want a stricter or looser list. On a municipality profile, the place count, flood share, protected share, website count and transit share follow your filters. Places per 1,000 residents, places per km2 and the ranks always use the default basis, so they can disagree with the count beside them. The CSV (comma-separated values) of one municipality's places follows your filters. The CSV of all municipalities (rankings and shading) uses the default basis. In the 2026-10 snapshot, a basis with no confidence cut and no worship holds 27,509 places.
caveats: The 0.50 cut is the observatory's own choice, not an Overture rule.
The cut matters. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the observatory counts 24,209 places at 0.50. With no cut and no places of worship it would count 27,509.
The cut removes more places of some types than others, and in the 2026-10 snapshot all 3,574 places below 0.50 are Meta records. See the confidence score entry.
The municipal land-use place shares (places_on_protected_land, places_on_protected_land_pct and places_urban_pct) do not follow this basis.
Folding duplicates can also remove places from the default count. See the duplicates entry.

places.barrio.plain: The barrio where the place's pin sits. A barrio is a sub-municipal district that the Census Bureau calls a county subdivision. Only places counted by default have one.
places.barrio.plain_es: El barrio donde está el marcador del lugar. Un barrio es una división dentro del municipio que el Negociado del Censo llama subdivisión de condado. Solo lo tienen los lugares que se cuentan con los filtros predeterminados.
places.barrio.definition: The name of the Census barrio (the Census Bureau calls it a county subdivision) that contains the pin. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 23,884 places have one: every place on the default basis except 325. Places of worship and places below the confidence cut have none.
places.barrio.method: Point-in-polygon test against Census barrio boundaries, run only for places counted by default (confidence 0.50 or higher, no places of worship). The first matching polygon is used. See 'How municipality and barrio are assigned to a place'.
places.barrio.how_to_read: Always read the barrio together with the municipality. Many barrio names repeat: in the barrio layer of the 2026-10 snapshot, 133 of the 694 barrio names occur in more than one municipality (for example Collores or Playa). Default basis means a confidence score of 0.50 or higher and no places of worship.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, 325 places on the default basis have no barrio because their pin falls in no barrio polygon. Almost all of them (323) are also outside the shoreline municipality polygons, that is offshore or at the shoreline.
The barrio is the Census Bureau's subdivision. It is not always the neighborhood name people use.
The place pop-up does not show the barrio. It is in the downloaded file and in the CSV (comma-separated values) download of a municipality's places.

places.withheld.plain: Why a place is counted in its municipality but not shown on the map: a holiday rental, or a rented unit named by its street address or unit number. Homes, housing and care services are not tourism and are not in the file at all (since 2026-10-18).
places.withheld.plain_es: Por qué un lugar se cuenta en su municipio, pero no aparece en el mapa: un alquiler vacacional, o una unidad alquilada cuyo nombre es su dirección o número de unidad. Las viviendas, los complejos de viviendas y los servicios de cuido no son turismo y no están en el archivo (desde el 2026-10-18).
places.withheld.definition: One of two reasons, present only on places the map does not draw: holiday_rental (a holiday rental: an entire home, cabin, cottage or apartment rented for short stays) and address (the name is a street address, a house, lot or unit number, or holds a postcode, and the listing is filed as a hotel, B&B, holiday rental, cabin or campground, or as a business such as a restaurant). In the 2026-10 snapshot, 1,005 of 32,541 places are withheld (holiday_rental 971, address 34), and 742 of them are among the 24,209 places on the default basis (holiday_rental 715, address 27). Three more reasons, residence (a private home, or a listing named after a private person), residential (a residential building, condominium, housing estate or subdivision, or a lodging listing that names no accommodation) and sensitive (an elderly or children's home, a shelter, rehabilitation or addiction treatment, a hospice and similar), and an address-named listing filed where homes are filed, mean the listing is not tourism: since 2026-10-18 it is left out of the file and of every count (HANDOFF decision 47). That left out 2,577 listings (residential 2,301, residence 157, address 67, sensitive 52), 2,370 of them on the default basis.
places.withheld.method: places_privacy.py decides from the Overture category and the name, with a reviewed list of exceptions (places_review.json): a sensitive word or a street address in the name withholds a place in any category; home words (Casa, Residencia, Hacienda, Villa...) and housing words (Urb., Residencial, Condominio, Apartments...) withhold it in the categories where Meta users file homes (lodging, historic site, park, beach and similar), unless the name also names an accommodation business or a public venue; and a lodging listing must name an accommodation. Holiday rentals (owner decision of 2026-10-18, HANDOFF decision 48) are withheld by category (holiday rental home, cabin, cottage, service apartment) and, in the lodging categories, by a name that says so (Vacation Rental, Beach House, Airbnb, Short Term Rental, Tiny House, ... Rentals, ... Stays) and, in the hotel, B&B, hostel and campground categories, by a name that rents a unit (... Apartment, Casita ..., Penthouse ..., Studio, Bungalow, Cabin, Chalet, Cottage, Villa 12, ... House, ... Home, ... Villa), a run of units (... Apartments, Condominio ...) or a house called Casa or Villa and one word, alone or followed by a town, municipio or neighbourhood, unless the name also names a hotel, guest house, inn, B&B, hostel, posada, parador or resort; hotels, guest houses, inns and B&Bs stay drawn, and real guest houses, hostels and aparthotels with such names are drawn by review. A home word followed by a unit or house number (Casa ... 28) withholds a place in any category. A listing withheld as residence, residential or sensitive, or as address in a category where homes are filed (lodging, historic site, park, beach and similar; a numbered holiday rental there is recorded as holiday_rental), is not tourism and is dropped before every count (places_privacy.not_tourism, decision 47 of 2026-10-18). A listing whose name also says holiday rental is recorded as holiday_rental (counted, not drawn) unless the name says housing clearly: a subdivision or estate word (Urb., Residencial, Estancias, Villas de...), a condominium or apartment building named as such (Condominio, Edificio, Torre), or a neighbourhood, sector or barrio of the gazetteer within 3 km. Outside the lodging category, Edificio, Edif. and Building alone do not say housing. A withheld place keeps the fields the counts use (municipality, barrio, category, type, Overture category, confidence, source, flood, protected-area, land-use and transit fields) and loses its name, Overture ID, coordinates, nearest stop and update date; its confidence is cut down to a multiple of 0.05, the step of the map's filter, and its distances to a stop and departures (transit_m here, ts_m, tw_m, ts_calls and tw_calls in place_access.json) to one value per class, so every count stays the same. The withheld rows come after all the drawn ones, sorted by their own fields, because Overture's order follows location. hub_400m (true or missing, only on a withheld place) says whether a rail station or ferry terminal is within 400 m, so the nightly transit refresh can still count the place. Owner rule of 2026-10-18; guide: docs/places-privacy.md.
places.withheld.how_to_read: These places are in every count and share (the Municipality tab, the choropleths of places shown, municipalities.json, barrios.geojson). They are not pins, hexagons, search results, list rows or CSV rows. They are tourism supply: 3.1% of the counted places in the 2026-10 snapshot. Until 2026-10-18 the counts also included the homes, housing and care services that Overture's sources filed under tourism categories: 2,370 of the 26,579 places then counted (8.9%). Since then they are left out, and every count and share was rebuilt without them (decision 47).
caveats: Overture gives no ownership or use field. The patterns can miss a home or hold back a public place; places_review.json lists the reviewed exceptions with their reasons.
A withheld place keeps the transit distances of the last full build: the nightly refresh cannot measure it again without its point.

values.holiday_rental: A holiday rental: an entire home, cabin, cottage or apartment rented for short stays, by its Overture category or a name that says so (971 in the 2026-10 snapshot). Hotels, guest houses, inns and B&Bs are drawn.
values.residence: A private home, or a listing named only after a private person. Not in the file since 2026-10-18: not tourism, so left out of every count (157 listings in the 2026-10 snapshot).
values.residential: A residential building, condominium, public housing estate or subdivision, or a lodging listing that names no accommodation. Not in the file since 2026-10-18: not tourism, so left out of every count (2,301 listings in the 2026-10 snapshot).
values.address: The name is a street address, a house, lot or unit number, or holds a postcode, and the listing is filed as a hotel, B&B, holiday rental, cabin or campground (a numbered unit rented to visitors) or as a business (34). The same names filed where homes are filed (lodging, historic site, park, beach and similar) are numbered homes and flats: not tourism, left out since 2026-10-18 (67).
values.sensitive: An elderly or children's home, a shelter, rehabilitation or addiction treatment, a hospice, a care, foster or recovery home (including one named 'Hogar ...' and filed under a lodging category) or a similar service. Not in the file since 2026-10-18: not tourism, so left out of every count (52 listings in the 2026-10 snapshot). The observatory publishes treatment facilities as counts only (community_series.json).

places.coordinates.plain: The position of the place's pin on the map, as latitude and longitude.
places.coordinates.plain_es: La posición del marcador del lugar en el mapa, en latitud y longitud.
places.coordinates.definition: Latitude and longitude of the listing's point, in decimal degrees (WGS 84, the World Geodetic System 1984 that GPS (Global Positioning System) and web maps use), rounded to 6 decimals. In the 2026-10 snapshot, latitudes run from 17.884134 to 18.515153 and longitudes from -67.940187 to -65.227658. The 1,005 places the map does not draw have no coordinates in the file (see Counted but not drawn).
places.coordinates.method: Copied from the Overture record's point and rounded to 6 decimals. Every flag in the file (municipality, barrio, flood zone, protected area, land-use class and transit distance) is computed from this point.
places.coordinates.how_to_read: The pin is where a source says the place is. It can sit on the street, at an entrance or in the middle of a lot.
caveats: Six decimals show the precision of the number, not the accuracy of the position. The source decides how accurate the pin is, and the observatory does not check it on the ground.
A place is one point. A beach, a river or a park appears as one pin, not as its shape or length.
Because every flag uses the pin, a pin a few meters off can change a flag, for example when it sits near the edge of a flood zone or a barrio.

In the 2026-10 snapshot, 2,012 of the 31,536 places with a pin (6.4%) share an exact pin with at least one other place, at 614 locations (up to 23 places on one pin). The distance-based flags treat such places as being at the same spot, and the map groups close pins into clusters, so the pins you can see are fewer than the places.

places.has_website.plain: Whether Overture lists a website for the place. The web address itself is not published.
places.has_website.plain_es: Si Overture da un sitio web para el lugar. La dirección del sitio web no se publica.
places.has_website.definition: true when the Overture record lists a website; missing otherwise. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 9,416 of 32,541 places (28.9%) are true, and 7,210 of 24,209 places on the default basis (29.8%).
places.has_website.method: Set by the build from the first website of the Overture record (websites[0]). The web address is not written to the file: the observatory publishes no business contact detail (owner rule of 2026-10-18; see Fields the observatory does not publish). Until 2026-10-18 the file published the address itself. A value that held an email address counts as no website (1 case in the 2026-10 snapshot).
places.has_website.how_to_read: A website means at least one source lists an online address for the place. It does not mean the place is open, that the site works or that it is the business's own site. Default basis means a confidence score of 0.50 or higher and no places of worship. The Municipality tab counts these places once the listings are loaded; before that it shows with_website from municipalities.json.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot as first built (35,118 places, before 2026-10-18), many listed websites were not a business's own site: 886 (9.1%) were Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube or X (Twitter) pages, 175 were Google Maps or goo.gl short links and 28 were WhatsApp links. The count of places with a website is therefore not a count of places with their own site.

In the 2026-10 snapshot, the municipal figure with_website adds up to the same 7,210 places on the default basis. Before 2026-10-18 it was one more than this field (7,441 against 7,440), because one website was counted before an email address was removed from it; that listing is no longer counted.

places.municipality.plain: The municipio where the place's pin sits, using Census boundaries. It can differ from the town named in the address.
places.municipality.plain_es: El municipio donde está el marcador del lugar, según los límites del Censo. Puede ser distinto del pueblo que aparece en la dirección.
places.municipality.definition: The name of one of Puerto Rico's 78 municipalities, spelled with accents (for example Bayamón or Mayagüez). Every place has one.
places.municipality.method: Point-in-polygon test of the pin against Census municipality boundaries that are generalized and clipped to the shoreline. A pin that falls in no boundary takes the municipality whose boundary is nearest (muni_locate.py); in the 2026-10 snapshot it took the nearest municipality center. See 'How municipality and barrio are assigned to a place'.
places.municipality.how_to_read: Use it to count or compare places by municipality. Every count of places per municipality in the observatory uses this field. Default basis means a confidence score of 0.50 or higher and no places of worship.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, the address names a different municipality than the one the pin falls in for 863 places (2.7% of the file). 325 places have no town in the address, and 590 more have a town text that is not one of the 78 municipality names.

Pins just offshore or at the shoreline can fall outside every boundary polygon. In the 2026-10 snapshot that is 348 places (1.1%). The 2026-10 build gave them the nearest municipality center, which can differ from the municipality next to the pin; the next full build gives them the nearest boundary, which moves 60 of them.
Boundaries are the Census Bureau's generalized lines, not legal survey lines.

A count of places is not a rate. Larger and more populous municipalities have more places: in the 2026-10 snapshot, San Juan has 3,424 places on the default basis and Maricao 36. To compare municipalities, use places per 1,000 residents or per km2. A rate per resident is high where visitors are many compared with residents.

places.oid.plain: A long code that identifies the place in Overture Maps. Use it to find the same place in Overture's own data.
places.oid.plain_es: Un código largo que identifica el lugar en Overture Maps. Sirve para encontrar el mismo lugar en los datos de Overture.
places.oid.definition: The Overture Maps identifier of the listing the observatory kept for the place: a 36-character code. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 31,536 places have one and all are different. The 1,005 places the map does not draw have none (see Counted but not drawn).
places.oid.method: Copied from the Overture record. When duplicate listings are folded into one place, the kept listing's ID is published and the IDs of the folded listings are not.
places.oid.how_to_read: Treat it as a label. The code says nothing about the place itself.
caveats: Overture sets its own rules for how an ID carries from one release to the next. Read Overture's documentation before you match the 2026-10 snapshot to another release.

The map's pop-ups do not show the ID. It is in the downloaded file and in the CSV (comma-separated values) download of a municipality's places. That CSV holds the places that pass your current filters.

places.name.plain: The name Overture lists for the place, as its sources wrote it. A place the map does not draw has no name in the file.
places.name.plain_es: El nombre que Overture da al lugar, tal como lo escribieron sus fuentes. Un lugar que el mapa no dibuja no tiene nombre en el archivo.
places.name.definition: Overture's primary name for the listing. Every place the map draws has one; the 1,005 places it does not draw have none (see Counted but not drawn). In the 2026-10 snapshot, the file holds 28,775 different names for 31,536 places, because chains such as fast-food brands have many outlets.
places.name.method: Copied from the Overture record (names.primary). The observatory does not translate names, fix spelling or change capital letters. It removes a telephone number or an email address written into a name (4 names held a telephone number in the 2026-10 snapshot).
places.name.how_to_read: The map search matches names. Two places can share a name, so use the place ID or the coordinates to tell them apart.
caveats: Some names carry extra words that a source added, such as a town or the country (in the 2026-10 snapshot, 537 names contain 'Puerto Rico' in any capital letters, for example 'Jardín Japonés, Ponce, Puerto Rico').
Spanish and English spellings both occur, so one place can be listed under different names. The observatory folds only some of these as duplicates.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, 353 names start or end with a blank space (351 end with one and 2 start with one), because the observatory does not clean names. Trim them before you match or join on name.

Names are copied as written, except that a telephone number or an email address is removed. A listing named only after a private person, or by a street address, and a holiday rental are not drawn and have no name in the file; a few names may still look like the names of individual professionals who run a business. Check a name before you republish it outside the observatory.

places.source.plain: The company or project that supplied the first source record Overture lists for the place.
places.source.plain_es: La empresa o el proyecto que aportó el primer registro de fuente que Overture tiene para el lugar.
places.source.definition: The name of the first data source in the Overture record. Four sources occur in the 2026-10 snapshot: Meta, Foursquare, Microsoft and AllThePlaces. Overture can merge records from several sources, so this is the first one listed. In the 2026-10 snapshot every place lists exactly one of these four sources next to Overture's own confidence-calculation record.
places.source.method: Copied from the first entry in the Overture record's list of sources (its dataset name). Every record also lists Overture's own confidence calculation, and in the 2026-10 snapshot 11 records add an Overture-signals entry (an Overture operating-status signal, with version dates 2026-05-11 and 2026-06-15). The observatory does not publish those entries.
places.source.how_to_read: Use it to say where a place record came from. The map pop-up shows it as the listing source.

places.duplicates.plain: How many other listings the observatory folded into this place because they looked like the same place. Most places have 0.

places.duplicates.definition: A whole number, 0 or more. A value above 0 means the place stands for that many extra listings that the observatory merged. In the 2026-10 snapshot, values run from 0 to 43, 691 places have at least one folded listing, and the folded listings add up to 1,005.
places.duplicates.method: Set by the de-duplication step: the size of the group of matching listings minus 1, because the kept listing is not counted. See 'How duplicate listings are folded'.
places.duplicates.how_to_read: The map pop-up says how many duplicate listings were folded. A high number often means a neighborhood or landmark name that many listings share, not one busy place. A value above 0 means listings were removed from the count. It does not mean the place is large or popular.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, places by number of folded listings: 0: 31,850; 1: 574; 2: 69; 3: 23. The largest values are 43 and 36, and 7 places have 10 or more.
Large groups can merge different places that share a neighborhood word. See 'How duplicate listings are folded'.

places.confidence.plain: Overture's own score, from 0 to 1, for a listing. The map's Map layers tab describes it as Overture's estimate that a listing is a real, current place. The observatory counts places at 0.50 or higher by default.
places.confidence.plain_es: La puntuación propia de Overture, de 0 a 1, para un listado. La pestaña Capas del mapa la describe como el estimado de Overture de que un listado es un lugar real y actual. El observatorio cuenta por defecto los lugares con 0.50 o más.
places.confidence.definition: A number from 0 to 1 with three decimals. In the 2026-10 snapshot, it runs from 0.024 to 1.000, the middle value is 0.83, 128 places score exactly 1, 14 score exactly 0.50 and 3,574 (11.0%) score below 0.50.
places.confidence.method: Copied from the Overture record and rounded to 3 decimals. Each record names an Overture 'confidence calculation' as the source of this value. In the 2026-10 snapshot, for 30,817 places (94.7%) it equals the score on the record from the contributing source (mostly Meta), and for the other 1,724 it differs. The observatory does not change it, except on a place the map does not draw (see Counted but not drawn): there the score is cut down to a multiple of 0.05, the step of the map's confidence filter (0.57 is written 0.55), so every count at every filter setting is the same and the exact score is not published. The figures in the definition are for the scores Overture gives.
places.confidence.how_to_read: A higher score means Overture is more confident in the listing. It is an estimate, not a rating of quality and not a measure of how many people visit.
caveats: The observatory does not check places on the ground, so a high score does not prove that a place is open today. The map's Map layers tab describes the score as an estimate that a listing is a real, current place.
The observatory's default cut at 0.50 is its own choice, not an Overture rule. See 'Which places the observatory counts'.

In the 2026-10 snapshot, all 3,574 listings below 0.50 are Meta records (11.2% of Meta's 31,945). No Foursquare, Microsoft or AllThePlaces record scores below 0.50, so the cut filters only Meta records.

In the 2026-10 snapshot, scores look different by source: 251 of 252 Foursquare places score exactly 0.77, 137 of 241 Microsoft places score 0.85 and 77 of 103 AllThePlaces places score 0.80, while Meta scores take 948 different values. The score does not rank places within those three sources.
The cut also removes more places of some types than others. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the 0.50 cut removes 27% of Vacation Properties and 3% of Beaches.

places.updated.plain: The date a data source last updated its record for the place. For most places it is the date of the source's data version, not the date anyone checked the place.

places.updated.definition: A date (YYYY-MM-DD) taken from the update time of the first source record in the Overture record. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the dates of the 31,536 places the map draws run from 2020-11-19 to 2026-09-14, 31,109 (98.6%) show a date in 2026, and 30,057 (95.3%) share the single date 2026-09-14. A place the map does not draw has no date in the file (see Counted but not drawn): with the other fields it could single the place out.
places.updated.method: The first 10 characters of the update time of the first source record in the Overture record.
places.updated.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot, for the 31,049 drawn places (98.5%) that come from Meta or AllThePlaces, the date equals the version label of the source record (for example 2026-09-14), so it marks a data version, not a visit to the place or a change to it. For Foursquare and Microsoft records the date differs from the version label. Do not use the date to judge whether a listing is current or stale.
caveats: A source can update a record without anyone visiting the place.
The map pop-up does not show this date. It is in the downloaded file and in CSV (comma-separated values) exports. The CSV of a municipality's places holds the places that pass your current filters.

It reads the key ATTRACTIONS of the field by_category in municipalities.json: counted places (confidence 0.50 or higher) that the observatory's keyword rules (RULES in build.py) put in the Attractions category, with places of worship left out. Types present: historic sites, parks, beaches, tourist attractions, cultural attractions (galleries, theatres, cinemas), scenic areas, museums and nature reserves. The Puerto Rico value is the sum of the 78 municipalities.
economy.attractions_places.method: site/js/economy.js, function ecLoad, helper snap. When the Analysis tab opens, the browser reads municipalities.json (key ATTRACTIONS of by_category) and builds a one-year series for each of the 78 municipalities. The Puerto Rico value is the sum of the 78 values. The only year is the year of the snapshot date in meta.json (2026 in the 2026-10 snapshot). Nothing is stored in economy_series.json. The observatory assigns each listing to the municipality whose boundary contains its map pin; a pin outside every boundary, such as one offshore, goes to the municipality whose boundary is nearest (see methods.municipality_assignment). See economy.tourism_supply_layers.
economy.attractions_places.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot, San Juan has the most (645), then Ponce 198, Carolina 157; the fewest are Las Marías and Naranjito, 12 each, then Florida 13. Divide by residents or land area before comparing places.
caveats: It counts listings, not businesses, rooms, beds or visitors. Overture builds its listings from several sources, and some are closed, moved, wrong or missing; the confidence score is Overture's and has not been checked on the ground.

Listings whose Overture category contains words such as church, chapel, temple or religious are left out of every count, even when a visitor would count a church as a sight. In the 2026-10 snapshot, that is 5,032 listings island-wide, including 1,169 religious organizations and 67 religious schools (see municipalities.counting_rules).

In the same snapshot, the type Tourist Attractions (783 listings) is a catch-all that includes, among the counted listings, arts and entertainment venues (234), stadiums and arenas (159), dance clubs (81), bridges (38) and casinos (26). The type Historic Sites is 22% of the category (1,010 listings), almost all of them Overture's generic 'historic site' label (952). The 24 counted listings that Overture classes as marinas (26 in the places file) are filed here, not under visitor services.
The de-duplication rules can leave two listings for one place (see municipalities.counting_rules), so the count is not a count of distinct sites.

The data come from Overture release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded on 1 October 2026. Listings were last updated by their sources between November 2020 and September 2026, so the count does not describe a single date.

There is only one snapshot, so these layers show no growth or decline. The tab's year control does not change them, and they have no 'change since the base year' option, no trend chart and no small trend line. The '% of the Puerto Rico total' option compares municipalities within the same snapshot.

economy.tourism_supply_layers.plain: The five tourism supply layers on the Analysis tab count Overture Maps listings in each municipality. The page works them out from the municipality data when the tab opens. They are not stored with the other Economy series.
economy.tourism_supply_layers.plain_es: Las cinco capas de oferta turística de la pestaña Análisis cuentan los listados de Overture Maps en cada municipio. La página las calcula a partir de los datos del municipio cuando se abre la pestaña. No se guardan con las otras series de Economía.
economy.tourism_supply_layers.definition: Five datasets in the Analysis tab's 'Tourism supply' group: economy.tourism_places (field assets), and economy.lodging_places, economy.gastronomy_places, economy.attractions_places and economy.visitor_services_places (the keys ACCOMMODATIONS, GASTRONOMY, ATTRACTIONS and VISITOR_SERVICES of the field by_category). Each is a count of listings per municipality in one snapshot. Each is marked 'static' in the code: it has one year, the year of the snapshot date, and the tab shows it whichever year is chosen.
economy.tourism_supply_layers.method: site/js/economy.js, function ecLoad, helper snap. Municipality values come from S.muni, which is municipalities.json read by the map page; the Puerto Rico value is the sum of the 78. The year of the series is the first four characters of generated_at in meta.json (2026 in the 2026-10 snapshot). Because each layer is static, the year control does not change it; 'change since the base year', the trend chart and the small trend line are not offered; and 'same classes in every year' does not apply. Options for counts: as published; per 1,000 residents (the default when shading; population from the Housing series for the latest year at or before the snapshot year, which is 2025 in the 2026-10 snapshot); per km² (land_km2 of municipalities.json); % of the Puerto Rico total; percentile among municipalities. The 'location quotient' and '% of the municipality's jobs' options are offered for jobs series only, not for these counts.
economy.tourism_supply_layers.how_to_read: Use these layers to see where visitor-facing places are concentrated, and put them next to jobs, income or hazard layers. Shade them per resident or per square kilometre, because raw counts mostly show which municipalities are big; raw counts suit sized symbols. The year control does not change these layers: when you pick an earlier year for another layer, you are pairing it with the listings of the 2026-10 snapshot.
caveats: They are not jobs, sales or visitors. For visitor-economy jobs see economy.tourism_jobs.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, the four category layers add up to the tourism places layer in every municipality.

The observatory holds one snapshot, so these layers have no earlier value to compare with. If a later snapshot is added, a change between snapshots will partly reflect changes in Overture's sources and in the observatory's rules, not only places opening or closing.

A listing is placed by its map pin; in the 2026-10 snapshot, 324 of the 24,209 counted listings have pins outside every municipal boundary and went to the municipality with the nearest centre; the next full build gives them the municipality whose boundary is nearest (see methods.municipality_assignment and municipalities.counting_rules).

Listings are not rooms or beds. A municipality with few listings can have large hotels.

economy.tourism_places.plain_es: Cuántos lugares turísticos lista Overture Maps en cada municipio: atracciones, restaurantes y barras, alojamientos y servicios para visitantes. Un lugar es un listado, no un negocio, una habitación ni una persona visitante.
economy.tourism_places.definition: The Analysis tab's 'Tourism places (all categories)' dataset. It reads the field assets of municipalities.json: de-duplicated Overture listings in the four categories (attractions, gastronomy, accommodations, visitor services), not places of worship, with an Overture confidence score of 0.50 or higher. The Puerto Rico value is the sum of the 78 municipalities.

When the Analysis tab opens, the browser reads municipalities.json (field assets) and builds a one-year series for each of the 78 municipalities. The Puerto Rico value is the sum of the 78 values. The only year is the year of the snapshot date in meta.json (2026 in the 2026-10 snapshot). Nothing is stored in economy_series.json. The observatory assigns each listing to the municipality whose boundary contains its map pin; a pin outside every boundary, such as one offshore, goes to the municipality whose boundary is nearest (see methods.municipality_assignment). economy.tourism_places.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot, San Juan has the most (3,424, 14.1% of the island) and Maricao the fewest (36). A shaded map of raw counts mostly shows which municipalities are big. On the Analysis tab, shading starts at 'per 1,000 residents', which divides by the latest population estimate in the Housing series (July 2025 in the 2026-10 snapshot); it differs slightly from municipalities.assets_per_1000_residents, which divides by the 2020 Census count. 'Per km²' divides by land area in square kilometres (municipalities.land_km2).
caveats: It counts listings, not businesses, rooms, beds or visitors. Overture builds its listings from several sources, and some are closed, moved, wrong or missing; the confidence score is Overture's and has not been checked on the ground.
Places of worship and listings with a confidence below 0.50 are left out, so the count is lower than the number of all listings (see municipalities.counting_rules).

In the 2026-10 snapshot, about two in three counted places are restaurants, bars and cafés (17,170 of 24,209), so this is not a measure of visitor demand. In the same snapshot, per-resident values are highest in small, visitor-heavy municipalities (Culebra 78.4, Vieques 30.1 and Rincón 28.4 per 1,000 residents, against 7.6 for Puerto Rico) because visitors and second-home owners are not in the denominator.

economy.visitor_services_places.plain: How many listings for services that visitors use (tour and adventure operators, airports and other transport, boat services, visitor centers) Overture Maps lists in each municipality. In the 2026-10 snapshot it is the smallest of the four tourism categories.
economy.visitor_services_places.plain_es: Cuántos listados de servicios para visitantes (operadores turísticos y de aventura, aeropuertos y otros medios de transporte, servicios de botes, centros de visitantes) lista Overture Maps en cada municipio. En el corte de datos de 2026-10 es la menor de las cuatro categorías turísticas.
