It reads the key VISITOR_SERVICES of the field by_category in municipalities.json: counted places (not places of worship, confidence 0.50 or higher) that the observatory's keyword rules (RULES in build.py) put in the Visitor Services category. The Puerto Rico value is the sum of the 78 municipalities. The category has six types: transportation (airports, bus stations, airport terminals, taxi services, heliports, limousine services and airport shuttles), adventure operators, tour operators, cultural experience providers, marinas and visitor centers.
economy.visitor_services_places.method: site/js/economy.js, function ecLoad, helper snap. When the Analysis tab opens, the browser reads municipalities.json (key VISITOR_SERVICES of by_category) and builds a one-year series for each of the 78 municipalities. The Puerto Rico value is the sum of the 78 values. The only year is the year of the snapshot date in meta.json (2026 in the 2026-10 snapshot). Nothing is stored in economy_series.json. The observatory assigns each listing to the municipality whose boundary contains its map pin; a pin outside every boundary, such as one offshore, goes to the municipality whose boundary is nearest (see methods.municipality_assignment). See economy.tourism_supply_layers.
economy.visitor_services_places.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot, the island has 617 listings of six types: transportation 173 (airports 112, bus stations 24, airport terminals 13, taxi services 10, heliports 8, limousine services 3 and airport shuttles 3), adventure operators 148, tour operators 116, cultural experience providers 101, marinas 74 and visitor centers 5. San Juan has the most (134), then Carolina 58, Fajardo 49. Nine municipalities have none: Aguas Buenas, Barranquitas, Corozal, Florida, Hormigueros, Juana Díaz, Maricao, San Lorenzo, San Sebastián. A zero here means Overture lists no such place in the counted set; it does not mean visitors cannot find these services there. With counts this small, one listing changes a municipality's rank a lot.
caveats: It counts listings, not businesses, rooms, beds or visitors. Overture builds its listings from several sources, and some are closed, moved, wrong or missing; the confidence score is Overture's and has not been checked on the ground.

The type names are the observatory's labels. In the 2026-10 snapshot, among the counted listings, all 101 cultural experience providers are dance studios; the 74 marinas are boat services (32), boat dealers (20), boat parts stores (14) and ferry companies (8); the 148 adventure operators include 23 surf stores (25 in the places file) and 21 equestrian facilities and horse trainers. Check the type before reading this layer as visitor demand.

The tab's description of this layer says 'tour operators, rentals, travel services'. The category holds the six types listed above. The counted set holds no car-rental listings: the observatory's classification rules read the word 'rental' as a vacation property first, and rentals that are not lodging are then left out (see places.classification). In the same snapshot, the transportation type is mostly airports, airport terminals and heliports (133 of 173). The observatory's rules put travel agencies under tour operators (4 of the 116 tour-operator listings). Lodging rentals are in the lodging layer, not here, and the 24 counted listings that Overture classes as marinas (26 in the places file) are filed under attractions.
Small counts: in the 2026-10 snapshot the island has only 617 listings, and 9 municipalities show 0.

municipalities.access_as_of.plain: The date against which the observatory judged whether each operator's timetable had ended when it computed the access fields. Quote it with any access figure.
municipalities.access_as_of.plain_es: La fecha con la que el observatorio juzgó si el horario de cada operador había terminado cuando calculó los campos de acceso. Cítela junto con cualquier cifra de acceso.
municipalities.access_as_of.definition: A date written YYYY-MM-DD. The observatory counts a stop as having a current timetable when its operator's feed end date is on or after this date. It applies to acc_cur400_pct, acc_cur800_pct, acc_freq400_pct, acc_sat400_pct, acc_sun400_pct, acc_paper_pct, stops_current and stops_expired. All 78 municipalities carry the same date. The same date is as_of in place_access.json and as_of in the access part of meta.json.
municipalities.access_as_of.method: access.py sets it to the build date at a full build and to the run date in the nightly refresh. When a run changes no value, the files are not rewritten and the date does not move.
municipalities.access_as_of.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot it is 2026-10-06, four days after the feeds were read (2026-10-02). A feed that ends after this date counts as current in the stored values. An older date means that no value has changed since then, not that the refresh did not run.
caveats: The stored values describe timetables on this date. They can be out of date by the time you read them if a feed has ended since and the next run has not written the change yet.
municipalities.access_as_of.source_detail: Overture Maps places (release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 1 October 2026; tourism places as classified by Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR)); stops and feed end dates from transport.json and operators.json (the GTFS, General Transit Feed Specification, timetable feeds of ATI, the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado, and of municipal systems, read on 2026-10-02); municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k, shoreline-clipped)

places.transit_m.plain: The straight-line distance in meters from the place to the nearest mapped stop, station or terminal of any kind in the observatory's stop data, including stops whose timetable has ended and stops that volunteers mapped. For the nearest stop with a current timetable, see ts_m.
places.transit_m.plain_es: La distancia en línea recta, en metros, desde el lugar hasta la parada, estación o terminal de cualquier tipo más cercana en los datos de paradas del observatorio, incluidas las paradas cuyo horario terminó y las que mapearon personas voluntarias. Para la parada más cercana con horario vigente, vea ts_m.
places.transit_m.definition: Whole meters (cut, not rounded) from the pin to the nearest stop of any kind in the observatory's list: scheduled bus, train and ferry stops from the timetables (GTFS, the General Transit Feed Specification) of ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) and of municipal systems, whether or not the timetable has ended, plus bus stops, bus stations, rail stations and ferry terminals mapped in OpenStreetMap. Every place has one. In the 2026-10 snapshot, values run from 0 to 77,841 m, and the middle value is 466 m (447 m on the places the map draws). On a place the map does not draw (see Counted but not drawn) the value is coarsened to one value per class, so that it cannot single the place out: 400 (within 400 m), 700 (more than 400 and less than 800), 800 (exactly 800, cut) or 1000 (more than 800). Every count and share reads the same class as before (owner decision of 2026-10-18).
places.transit_m.method: access.py compares each place with every stop of kind transit stop, bus stop, bus station, rail station or ferry terminal, finds the nearest in meters with a flat-earth formula (111,320 m per degree of latitude, with longitude shortened by the cosine of the mean latitude) and cuts the distance to whole meters. Airports, helipads, taxi stands and electric-vehicle chargers are not counted as stops.
places.transit_m.how_to_read: A smaller number means a stop of some kind is closer. 400 m (a quarter mile) is the planning distance for a walk to a bus stop. This is the distance to any mapped stop, which can be a stop whose timetable has ended or one that volunteers mapped. For the nearest stop with a current timetable, use ts_m in place_access.json. The map pop-up shows it on the line 'Any mapped stop (expired timetables and volunteer-mapped stops included)', as meters or kilometers, when a stop without a current timetable is closer than the nearest stop with one. Hovering over that line shows the stop's name. Earlier versions of the observatory labelled the field 'distance to the nearest transit stop'.
caveats: In the 2026-10 access update the field was recomputed from today's stop list for all places: 1,204 of the 35,118 places changed, 892 of them by more than 2 m (always shorter), among them all 183 places in Jayuya. See municipalities.transit_data_updates.
It is a straight line, not a walking route. Rivers, highways and hills are ignored.

A stop counts if it is on the list, even when its timetable has expired or when it comes from OpenStreetMap and has no timetable. A stop on the list is not always served today. In the 2026-10 snapshot 3,717 of the 11,507 default-basis places within 400 m of a stop have no stop with a current timetable within 400 m.
The nearest stop is found by comparing the distance in meters to every stop, so the stop named in nearest_stop is the nearest by the formula above.
The field is recomputed from the stop list at each full build and at each run of the nightly transit refresh, so it follows the stops shown on the map.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, the largest values (68,541 to 77,841 m) belong to the four places on Mona Island.

The stop list mixes sources with different terms: the ATI feed (provided as is, with no warranty), municipal GTFS feeds (no license stated) and OpenStreetMap (Open Database License, ODbL; credit OpenStreetMap contributors). Check each source's terms before you reuse stop names or distances.

place_access.ts_m.plain: How far, in a straight line, a tourism place is from the nearest stop whose published timetable has not ended. It is the distance behind the access class in the map pop-up.
place_access.ts_m.plain_es: Qué tan lejos, en línea recta, está un lugar turístico de la parada más cercana cuyo horario publicado no ha terminado. Es la distancia en la que se basa la clase de acceso de la ventana emergente del mapa.
place_access.ts_m.definition: Meters from the place's map point to the nearest scheduled stop whose operator's timetable feed has an end date on or after the as-of date (the field as_of of place_access.json). A scheduled stop is a stop in the timetable feed (GTFS, the General Transit Feed Specification) of ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) or of a municipal transit system. Stops of feeds that have ended, stops that volunteers mapped in OpenStreetMap, airports, taxi stands and chargers are not used. The distance is rounded up to whole meters, so a value of 400 or less is exactly the test behind the shares of places near a stop with a current timetable. 99,999 is the largest value the file can hold. The file has one value for each place of places.json, in the same order. It carries no place ids, so a page joins the two files by position and checks that its count n equals the number of places and that the build time in its field built matches generated_at in meta.json. On a place the map does not draw (see Counted but not drawn) the value is coarsened to one value per class: 400 (400 m or less), 800 (more than 400, up to 800), 1000 (more than 800, up to 1,000) or 99,999 (more than 1,000); every count and share reads the same class as before (owner decision of 2026-10-18).
place_access.ts_m.method: access.py compares every place with every scheduled stop of an operator whose feed has not ended, in blocks of 500 places. It uses the flat-earth formula that the observatory uses everywhere (111,320 m per degree of latitude, longitude shortened by the cosine of the mean latitude), keeps the smallest distance and rounds it up. A feed counts as current when its end date (feed.end in operators.json) is on or after the as-of date; a feed with no end date does not count. The as-of date is the build date at a full build and the run date in the nightly refresh. Against a computation in projected meters the formula is about 0.6% long north to south, so a share can read up to 0.1 point lower (32.0% instead of 32.1% of places near a stop with a current timetable).
place_access.ts_m.how_to_read: A smaller number means a stop whose timetable is still in force is closer. 400 m or less is the test for a stop within 400 m; 400 to 800 m is the 'Stop 400–800 m away' class of the pop-up. It says how far the stop is. It does not say how often vehicles come (see ts_calls), whether the walk is safe, or that the service runs today. In the 2026-10 snapshot the middle value is 3,924 m across all 32,541 places. 10,491 places (32.2%) are 400 m or less from such a stop, and so are 7,790 of the 24,209 places on the default basis (32.2%). For the nearest stop of any kind, use transit_m.
caveats: Straight line, not a walking route. It ignores hills, rivers, highways and fences. The walk along mapped roads is place_access.tw_m, which the map's access classes use.
A stop with a current timetable is not proof of service. A timetable is a schedule: it does not show that vehicles run on time or at all. The observatory has no real-time data.

Stops of expired timetables are left out. In the 2026-10 snapshot 966 stops of 7 operators have an expired timetable (Ponce ended 2024-12-31, Hatillo 2025-12-31, Cidra 2026-01-15, Caguas 2026-01-31, San Lorenzo 2026-02-28, Fajardo 2026-06-15 and Juncos 2026-07-31). Buses can still run there, so a long distance near one of these towns can reflect a feed that was not renewed, not a lack of service.
Públicos (shared taxis and vans), taxis, ride-hailing, rental cars and tour shuttles are in no timetable, so they are not counted.
The values change on the day a feed ends. In the 2026-10 snapshot 9 of the 18 current feeds end between 2026-10-31 and 2027-01-31, among them San Juan's municipal feed (see methods.access_profile).
The nearest stop can lie in another municipality.
ts_m is rounded up and transit_m is cut to whole meters, so for the same stop the two can differ by 1 m.
In the 2026-10 snapshot the largest values (68,542 to 77,943 m) belong to the four places on Mona Island.
Each distance starts at the place's listed point, which can be wrong in the source (Overture Maps).

Stops: scheduled stops in transport.json (the GTFS, General Transit Feed Specification, timetable feeds of ATI, the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado, and of municipal systems, read on 2026-10-02). Feed end dates: operators.json.

methods.access_profile.plain: The observatory describes a tourism place's access to transport as a profile, not a score: the nearest stop whose timetable has not ended, how many weekday departures it has and whether it has weekend service. Walking distance and gateways such as airports and ferry terminals are planned and not published yet.
methods.access_profile.plain_es: El observatorio describe el acceso de un lugar turístico al transporte como un perfil, no como una puntuación: la parada más cercana cuyo horario no ha terminado, cuántas salidas tiene en días de semana y si tiene servicio el fin de semana. La distancia a pie y los puntos de entrada, como los aeropuertos y las terminales de lanchas, están planificados y aún no se publican.
methods.access_profile.definition: The profile has three layers. Layer 1 is published: the straight-line distance to the nearest stop with a current timetable (ts_m), the most weekday calls at such a stop within 400 m (ts_calls) and the Saturday and Sunday service at those stops (ts_we). The stops come from the GTFS (General Transit Feed Specification) timetable feeds of ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) and of the municipal transit systems. Layer 2, the walking distance along mapped roads, and layer 3, the nearest gateways (airport, ferry terminal, rail station and bus terminal) and scheduled journey times from a gateway, are planned. They are not published, and nothing in the map or the data files measures them yet. From layer 1 each place falls in one of five access classes, which use the distances 400 m and 800 m and the threshold of 20 weekday calls (see Codes). The older measure, within 400 m of any mapped stop (transit_m, transit_400m and transit_pct), stays and is labelled as what it is: it also counts stops whose timetable has ended and stops that volunteers mapped. The pop-up of a place shows the class as a badge, then the line 'Nearest stop with a current timetable' with its distance (and, within 400 m, the weekday departures and the weekend service). A third line, 'Any mapped stop (expired timetables and volunteer-mapped stops included)', appears when such a stop is closer than the nearest stop with a current timetable.
methods.access_profile.method: access.py computes the profile from places.json, transport.json and operators.json. A stop has a current timetable when it is a scheduled stop (source ATI or a municipal GTFS feed) and its operator's feed end date is on or after the as-of date; a feed with no end date does not count. For every place it finds the nearest such stop (ts_m, rounded up to whole metres), the largest number of weekday calls at such stops within 400 m (ts_calls) and the Saturday and Sunday flags (ts_we). It also finds the nearest mapped stop of any kind (transit_m, cut to whole metres, and the flag transit_400m). Distances are straight lines from the flat-earth formula that the observatory has always used. Against a computation in projected metres the formula is about 0.6% long north to south, so a share can read up to 0.1 point lower than a projected computation (32.0% instead of 32.1% of places within 400 m of a stop with a current timetable). Shares count the default basis: tourism places with confidence 0.50 or higher and no places of worship. The municipal fields, the barrio counts and the access part of meta.json add up the same flags. The class of a place follows access_class in access.py, and the map applies the same rule in site/js/access.js.
methods.access_profile.how_to_read: Read it as a profile: first the distance, then how often, then weekends. The observatory does not combine them into one score. A score would need weights (how much a Saturday service is worth against a closer stop), and the weights would be a policy choice that has not been made. A score would also hide the main finding: in the 2026-10 snapshot 64% of the 24,209 places on the default basis have no stop with a current timetable within 800 m. Island figures on the default basis, as of 2026-10-06: 47.5% of places are within 400 m of any mapped stop and 32.2% of a stop with a current timetable; 21.3% are within 400 m of a frequent stop; 22.4% are within 400 m of a stop with Saturday service and 6.4% of one with Sunday service. Of the 11,507 places within 400 m of any mapped stop, 7,790 (67.7%) have a stop with a current timetable and 3,717 (32.3%) rest on stops whose timetable has ended or that have none.
caveats: Schedule-based, not real time. The observatory has no live vehicle positions. A stop with a current timetable is a stop in a published schedule, not proof that vehicles run, on time or at all.
Straight line, not walking distance. It ignores hills, rivers, highways, fences and missing sidewalks. A walking distance along mapped roads would be an estimate, and it is not published yet.
Públicos (shared taxis and vans), taxis, ride-hailing, rental cars and tour shuttles are in no timetable. A place with no stop within 800 m can still be reachable by them.

Missing is not zero. A feed with no weekend calls does not prove that there is no weekend service, and a municipality with no feed does not lack transport. In the 2026-10 snapshot 25 operators publish a feed (ATI and 24 municipal systems). No feed was found for 15 municipal systems and the públicos authority. Only 3 of the 18 current feeds list Saturday calls and only 1 lists Sunday calls.

An expired timetable is not an absence of buses. Ponce's figures (0.1% of its places within 400 m of a stop with a current timetable, 79.1% within 400 m of any mapped stop) reflect a feed that ended on 2024-12-31. Do not compare municipalities as if their feeds were equally complete.

The profile depends on the date. It is computed as of a date (2026-10-06 in the 2026-10 snapshot) and changes on the day a feed ends: 9 of the 18 current feeds end between 2026-10-31 and 2027-01-31, among them San Juan's municipal feed on 2027-01-31. Computed as of 2027-02-01 with the same feeds, 26.1% of the places would be within 400 m of a stop with a current timetable, instead of 32.2%. That is arithmetic on the end dates, not a forecast of service: operators can publish new feeds.
Weekday calls are a proxy for frequency, not a headway (the time between vehicles). The busiest single stop within 400 m is used, not the sum of the stops.
Counts are listings from Overture Maps, not businesses, rooms or visitors. The distance is measured from a place's listed point.
The barrio counts are rebuilt only at a full build, so between full builds they can lag the municipal fields.

values.Frequent stop within 400 m: A stop with a current timetable is 400 m or less away and the busiest such stop within 400 m has 20 or more weekday calls. 5,163 places (21.3%) in the 2026-10 snapshot.
values.Stop within 400 m: A stop with a current timetable is 400 m or less away, and the busiest such stop within 400 m has fewer than 20 weekday calls. 2,627 places (10.9%).
values.Stop 400–800 m away: The nearest stop with a current timetable is more than 400 m and at most 800 m away. 964 places (4.0%).
values.Only expired or unscheduled stops within: No stop with a current timetable within 800 m, but a mapped stop within 800 m: a stop whose timetable has ended, or one that volunteers mapped, with no timetable. 4,690 places (19.4%).
values.No stop within 800 m: No mapped stop of any kind within 800 m. 10,765 places (44.5%).

places.nearest_stop.plain: The name of the stop, station or terminal of any kind that is closest to the place, whether or not its timetable has ended.
places.nearest_stop.plain_es: El nombre de la parada, estación o terminal de cualquier tipo más cercana al lugar, haya terminado o no su horario.
places.nearest_stop.definition: The name of the nearest stop used for the transit distance (transit_m). When the stop has no name, the text is its kind, such as bus stop. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 3,020 different values occur. A place the map does not draw has none (see Counted but not drawn).
places.nearest_stop.method: Taken from the stop found for transit_m: its name, or its kind with underscores replaced by spaces when it has no name.
places.nearest_stop.how_to_read: The map shows it as a tooltip on the 'Any mapped stop' line of a pop-up. Many names are terminals, for example públicos terminals. It names the nearest stop of any kind, which may have no current timetable. The observatory does not publish the name of the nearest stop with a current timetable.
caveats: In the 2026-10 access update the names were recomputed from today's stop list. The 183 places in Jayuya now name stops of Jayuya's own feed; before, all 183 named a stop in another municipality because 58 Jayuya stops had a wrong longitude.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, 1,041 of the places the map draws show only 'bus stop', 85 show 'bus station' and 57 show 'ferry terminal', because the nearest stop has no name in its source.
Names are as the feeds or OpenStreetMap wrote them, in Spanish or English. The observatory does not check that a stop is in service.

place_access.tw_straight.plain: The list of places that have no mapped road within 150 m, so their walking fields keep the straight-line values. The map pop-up says so for these places.
place_access.tw_straight.plain_es: La lista de los lugares que no tienen una calle mapeada a 150 m o menos, así que sus campos a pie conservan los valores en línea recta. La ventana del mapa lo dice para estos lugares.
place_access.tw_straight.definition: Positions (0-based, in the order of places.json) of the places whose map point has no walkable road of roads.bin within 150 m. For each of them tw_m equals ts_m, tw_calls equals ts_calls and tw_we equals ts_we.
place_access.tw_straight.method: walknet.py snaps each place to the nearest road of the walking network within 150 m (shapely's nearest-geometry search). A place with no road in that distance is listed here and access.py copies its straight-line values.
place_access.tw_straight.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot 1,210 places are listed, 1,074 of them on the default basis (4.4%): 622 attractions, 325 gastronomy places, 78 visitor services and 49 accommodations. The most are in San Juan (114), Carolina (103), Fajardo (63) and Ponce (59). Beaches, trails and parks inside large grounds are typical. For these places the walking share counts the straight line, which can only understate the walk.
caveats: 150 m is the connector the visitor-access study tested, not a standard. A wider limit would join more places to a road across a barrier.
A place can be on a footpath, a beach or a private road that the road file does not hold.

municipalities.access_n.plain: How many tourism places the access shares of the municipality are based on. It is the number each acc_ percentage divides by.
municipalities.access_n.plain_es: Cuántos lugares turísticos sirven de base para las proporciones de acceso del municipio. Es el número entre el cual se divide cada porcentaje acc_.
municipalities.access_n.definition: The number of tourism places in the municipality that every access share (transit_pct and the acc_ fields) divides by: places with confidence 0.50 or higher and a type other than Places of Worship, located in the municipality. It is the same set as assets and equals assets in all 78 municipalities.
municipalities.access_n.method: access.py counts the places on the default basis in each municipality when it computes the shares.
municipalities.access_n.how_to_read: Read it before you compare shares: a share of a municipality with few places can swing widely. In the 2026-10 snapshot the values add up to 24,209 and range from 36 to 3,424 (San Juan). Multiply a share by this number and divide by 100 to get the number of places, to the nearest place. The Municipality tab's live tiles use the places that pass your filters, not this number.
caveats: Counts are listings from Overture Maps, not businesses, rooms or visitors.
A place outside every municipality boundary takes the municipality whose boundary is nearest (in the 2026-10 snapshot, the nearest centre; see methods.municipality_assignment).

municipalities.acc_freq400_pct.plain: Out of every 100 tourism places in the municipality, how many are within 400 m of a stop with a current timetable and 20 or more weekday departures. It is a rough sign of frequent service.
municipalities.acc_freq400_pct.plain_es: De cada 100 lugares turísticos del municipio, cuántos están a 400 m o menos de una parada con horario vigente y 20 o más salidas en días de semana. Es una señal aproximada de servicio frecuente.
municipalities.acc_freq400_pct.definition: The number of tourism places in the municipality whose distance to the nearest stop with a current timetable is 400 m or less and whose largest number of weekday calls at such a stop within 400 m (ts_calls) is 20 or more, divided by the tourism places counted (access_n), times 100, rounded to one decimal. A call is one stop time in the timetable; the app calls them departures (see place_access.ts_calls). 20 is a threshold chosen for the observatory, not a standard.
municipalities.acc_freq400_pct.method: access.py counts the places with ts_m of 400 or less and ts_calls of 20 or more in each municipality and divides by the counted places.
municipalities.acc_freq400_pct.how_to_read: A high value means most of the municipality's visitor places have a busy stop nearby. It is a proxy for frequency, not a headway (the time between vehicles): the calls are spread over a whole weekday, and 20 calls can be a bus every hour or a few buses in the morning and evening. In the 2026-10 snapshot the value is 21.3% island-wide (5,163 of 24,209 places) and ranges from 0.0 to 77.6 (San Juan). 59 of the 78 municipalities have 0.0 and 19 have a value above 0. The Municipality tab shows a live share of the places that pass your filters, not this stored field.
caveats: A stop with a current timetable is not proof of service. It shows that a schedule is published, not that vehicles run on time or at all. The observatory has no real-time data.
Weekday calls describe a typical Wednesday. Holidays and other exceptions in the feeds are not applied (see transit.typical_weekday).
Públicos (shared taxis and vans), taxis, ride-hailing, rental cars and tour shuttles are in no timetable, so they are not counted.
The values change on the day a feed ends. In the 2026-10 snapshot 9 of the 18 current feeds end between 2026-10-31 and 2027-01-31, among them San Juan's municipal feed (see methods.access_profile).
A municipality with few places can swing widely: the smallest has 36 places, so one place is 2.8 points. Check access_n before you compare shares.

A municipality with no stop counted inside its border (14 in the 2026-10 snapshot) holds the stored value: 0.0, or a small value where a place lies near a stop in a neighbouring municipality (for example 0.5 for Toa Alta). That is not a measured 0%. The 2D map leaves it unshaded and unranked, and the downloaded municipality table leaves it blank.

boundaries.barrio_acc_freq400.plain: How many of the barrio's tourism places are within 400 m of a stop with a current timetable and 20 or more weekday departures. It is a rough sign of frequent service.
boundaries.barrio_acc_freq400.plain_es: Cuántos de los lugares turísticos del barrio están a 400 m o menos de una parada con horario vigente y 20 salidas o más en un día laborable. Es una señal aproximada de servicio frecuente.
boundaries.barrio_acc_freq400.definition: Count of tourism places in the barrio (see boundaries.barrio_assets) that have a stop with a current timetable within 400 m and for which the busiest such stop within 400 m has 20 or more weekday calls (ts_m of 400 or less and ts_calls of 20 or more in place_access.json). A call is one stop time in the timetable; the app calls them departures. 20 is a threshold chosen for the observatory, not a standard.
boundaries.barrio_acc_freq400.method: build_barrios in landuse.py adds one for each counted place (confidence 0.50 or higher, no places of worship) whose pin lies in the barrio and whose access flag freq400 is true, from access.py.
boundaries.barrio_acc_freq400.how_to_read: A high number means many of the barrio's places have a busy stop nearby. It is a proxy for frequency, not a headway (the time between vehicles). In the 2026-10 snapshot values run from 0 to 1,205 (Santurce, San Juan) and add up to 5,120. 67 of the 901 barrios have a value above 0. The barrio total is lower than the island count (5,163) because 43 places near a frequent stop fall in no barrio.
caveats: Straight-line distance, not a walking route.
A stop with a current timetable is not proof of service. It shows that a schedule is published, not that vehicles run on time or at all. The observatory has no real-time data.
A barrio with 0 can sit in a municipality whose operator did not renew its feed, or in one with no feed. It does not show that no vehicle runs.
Públicos (shared taxis and vans), taxis, ride-hailing and rental cars are in no timetable, so they are not counted.
Weekday calls describe a typical Wednesday. Holidays and other exceptions in the feeds are not applied (see transit.typical_weekday).
The values keep the access date of the last full build.

municipalities.acc_hub400_pct.plain: Out of every 100 tourism places in the municipality, how many are within 400 m of a train station or a ferry terminal. It marks places near a rail or boat connection.
municipalities.acc_hub400_pct.plain_es: De cada 100 lugares turísticos del municipio, cuántos están a 400 m o menos de una estación de tren o una terminal de lanchas. Señala los lugares cerca de una conexión por tren o por lancha.
municipalities.acc_hub400_pct.definition: The number of tourism places in the municipality whose distance to the nearest rail station or ferry terminal is 400 m or less, divided by the tourism places counted (access_n), times 100, rounded to one decimal. The stations and terminals come from any source: the timetable feeds of ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) and OpenStreetMap, whatever the state of the timetable. Bus stations and airports are not counted.
municipalities.acc_hub400_pct.method: access.py tests the distance from each place to every point of kind rail station or ferry terminal in transport.json, counts the places within 400 m in each municipality and divides by the counted places.
municipalities.acc_hub400_pct.how_to_read: A high value means many of the municipality's visitor places are near a station or terminal where a train or a boat starts. It does not say whether service runs, or whether the connection leads where a visitor wants to go. In the 2026-10 snapshot the value is 2.9% island-wide (695 of 24,209 places) and ranges from 0.0 to 23.5 (Culebra). Only 9 municipalities have a value above 0: Culebra 23.5, Cataño 16.2, San Juan 14.5, Vieques 11.4, Bayamón 9.5, Ceiba 2.3, Fajardo 1.7, Guaynabo 1.7 and Arecibo 0.5.
caveats: The ferry terminals include volunteer-mapped points. For example, a cruise-ship pier in San Juan counts (see municipalities.ferry_terminals).
A rail station or ferry terminal can have an expired timetable, or none. Read this field with acc_cur400_pct.

municipalities.acc_cur400_pct.plain: Out of every 100 tourism places in the municipality, how many are within 400 m, in a straight line, of a stop whose published timetable has not ended. It measures places, not residents.
municipalities.acc_cur400_pct.plain_es: De cada 100 lugares turísticos del municipio, cuántos están a 400 m o menos, en línea recta, de una parada cuyo horario publicado no ha terminado. Mide lugares, no residentes.
municipalities.acc_cur400_pct.definition: The number of tourism places in the municipality whose distance to the nearest stop with a current timetable (ts_m in place_access.json) is 400 m or less, divided by the tourism places counted (access_n, equal to assets), times 100, rounded to one decimal. A stop with a current timetable is a scheduled stop of ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) or of a municipal transit system whose operator's feed has an end date on or after access_as_of. The stop can be in another municipality.
municipalities.acc_cur400_pct.method: access.py counts the places with ts_m of 400 or less in each municipality (a place belongs to the municipality where its point falls) and divides by the counted places. Stops of feeds that have ended, volunteer-mapped stops, airports, taxi stands and chargers are not used. See place_access.ts_m for how the distance is found.
municipalities.acc_cur400_pct.how_to_read: A high value means most of the municipality's visitor places are close to a stop that has a timetable in force. It shows where such stops are. It does not show how often vehicles come (see acc_freq400_pct) or that the service runs today. Compare it with transit_pct (any mapped stop): the gap is the places near only a stop with an ended timetable or none (acc_paper_pct). In the 2026-10 snapshot the value is 32.2% island-wide (7,790 of 24,209 places) and ranges from 0.0 to 93.3 (San Juan). 47 of the 78 municipalities have 0.0 and 13 have 50% or more. The Municipality tab shows a live share of the places that pass your filters, not this stored field.
caveats: Straight-line distance, not a walking route (see municipalities.walk_rule_400m). The share by walking along mapped roads is in the acc_walk fields (acc_walk400_pct, acc_walk800_pct, acc_wfreq400_pct).
A stop with a current timetable is not proof of service. It shows that a schedule is published, not that vehicles run on time or at all. The observatory has no real-time data.
Públicos (shared taxis and vans), taxis, ride-hailing, rental cars and tour shuttles are in no timetable, so they are not counted.

A low value can mean that the operator did not renew its feed, not that no buses run. In the 2026-10 snapshot 7 of the 25 feeds have ended, and no feed was found for 15 municipal systems and the públicos authority.

municipalities.transit_pct.plain: Out of every 100 tourism places in the municipality, how many stand within 400 m (a quarter mile), in a straight line, of any mapped stop, station or terminal, including stops whose timetable has ended and stops that volunteers mapped. It measures places, not residents.
municipalities.transit_pct.plain_es: De cada 100 lugares turísticos del municipio, cuántos están a 400 m o menos (un cuarto de milla), en línea recta, de cualquier parada, estación o terminal registrada en el mapa, incluidas las paradas cuyo horario terminó y las que registraron personas voluntarias. Mide lugares, no residentes.
municipalities.transit_pct.definition: places_near_transit divided by assets (the tourism places counted in the municipality: confidence 0.50 or higher, places of worship left out), times 100, rounded to one decimal. The denominator is tourism places, not residents. In the file the value is never empty: a municipality with no transit stops (transit_stops = 0) holds 0.0, or a small value when a place lies near a stop in a neighbouring municipality.
municipalities.transit_pct.method: places_near_transit divided by the number of counted tourism places, times 100.
municipalities.transit_pct.how_to_read: A high value means most of the municipality's visitor places are close to a mapped stop. It is a measure of where stops are, not of service: a stop with one bus a day counts the same as a station, and a stop whose timetable has ended counts as well. For places near a stop whose timetable has not ended, use acc_cur400_pct; the difference between the two is acc_paper_pct. In the 2D map a municipality with no mapped stops has no colour or rank, for this share and for the access shares; the 0.0 stored for it is not a measured 0%. The municipality panel in the map recomputes the share from the places that pass your current filters, so it can differ from this field. In the 2026-10 snapshot the file ranges from 0.0 to 95.4 (San Juan); island-wide, 47.5%.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, the 14 municipalities with transit_stops = 0 hold 0.0 in the file, except Toa Alta (0.5) and Arroyo (0.9), where one place lies near a stop in a neighbouring municipality. The 2D map and the downloaded municipality table show these as no data; the Housing page profile and the 3D map show the stored values, which are not a measured transit share.

A municipality with only one or two mapped stops still gets a percentage. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 24 municipalities have exactly one stop. In 20 of them it is a single volunteer-mapped bus station, mostly a carros públicos (shared taxi) terminal (for example Sabana Grande 40.7%, Camuy 16.0%). Read such values as "near that one terminal", not as transit coverage.

transit_pct counts volunteer-mapped stops and stops of ended timetables; pop_served_pct counts scheduled stops only. In the 2026-10 snapshot Mayagüez shows 23.9% and 0.2%. Do not compare the two. For a like-for-like comparison use acc_cur400_pct (places) with pop_served_active_pct (residents): both need a timetable that has not ended.
Straight-line distance, not a walking route. See municipalities.walk_rule_400m.
Share of tourism places, not of residents. For residents use pop_served_active_pct or pop_served_pct.

Licenses differ by source: volunteer-mapped OpenStreetMap stops carry the ODbL (Open Database License), the municipal feeds state no license, and the feed of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) is provided as is. Check each source's terms before reusing the stops.
The values are recomputed from the stops file at each full build and at each run of the nightly refresh. The barrio counts (boundaries.barrio_transit) are rebuilt only at a full build.
In the 2026-10 access update the value for Jayuya changed from 0.0 to 70.7 and the value for Ponce from 79.0 to 79.1; see municipalities.transit_data_updates.

municipalities.places_near_transit.plain: How many of the municipality's tourism places stand within 400 m (a quarter mile), in a straight line, of any mapped stop, station or terminal: one in a timetable (even a timetable that has ended) or one that volunteers mapped. It does not show that vehicles run.
municipalities.places_near_transit.plain_es: Cuántos de los lugares turísticos del municipio están a 400 m o menos (un cuarto de milla), en línea recta, de cualquier parada, estación o terminal registrada en el mapa: una que esté en un horario (aunque ese horario haya terminado) o una que registraron personas voluntarias. No demuestra que haya vehículos en servicio.
municipalities.places_near_transit.definition: Among the tourism places counted in the municipality (field assets: places with confidence 0.50 or higher, places of worship left out), the number whose nearest transit stop, bus station, rail station or ferry terminal is 400 m or less away in a straight line. The stops are those of transit_stops: scheduled and OpenStreetMap-mapped, any operator, in any municipality, including feeds whose timetable has ended. Airports, taxi stands and electric-vehicle (EV) chargers are not used. For the places near a stop whose timetable has not ended, see acc_cur400_pct.
municipalities.places_near_transit.method: access.py measures the straight-line distance from every place to every stop of kind transit stop, bus stop, bus station, rail station or ferry terminal, takes the nearest in metres and flags the place when it is 400 m or less (the flag is transit_400m in places.json). A place belongs to the municipality where its point falls. The field counts the flagged places among the municipality's counted tourism places.
municipalities.places_near_transit.how_to_read: It counts places near a mapped stop. It shows where stops are, not where service runs today, because it counts stops whose timetable has ended and stops that volunteers mapped. Earlier versions of the observatory labelled it 'within 400 m of transit'. For places near a stop with a timetable in force, use acc_cur400_pct. To compare municipalities of different size, use transit_pct, which divides this count by the tourism places in assets. It says nothing about service frequency, hours or the route a person would walk. The Municipality tab's "places within 400 m of any mapped stop" tile in the map is a live percentage of the places you have filtered, not this stored count. In the 2026-10 snapshot the island total is 11,507 of 24,209 tourism places.
caveats: Straight-line distance ignores hills, fences, rivers and street crossings. See municipalities.walk_rule_400m.
A stop in a neighbouring municipality counts for a place near the border.

It counts stops of timetables that have ended and volunteer-mapped stops. In the 2026-10 snapshot 3,717 of the 11,507 places have no stop with a current timetable within 400 m (see acc_paper_pct). OpenStreetMap coverage is uneven.

Licenses differ by source: volunteer-mapped OpenStreetMap stops carry the ODbL (Open Database License), the municipal feeds state no license, and the feed of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) is provided as is. Check each source's terms before reusing the stops.

The values are recomputed from the stops file at each full build and at each run of the nightly refresh, which also updates the places' own nearest-stop fields. The barrio counts are rebuilt only at a full build.

municipalities.acc_paper_pct.plain: Out of every 100 tourism places in the municipality, how many are within 400 m of a mapped stop but of no stop with a current timetable. The stop's timetable has ended, or volunteers mapped the stop and no timetable exists.
municipalities.acc_paper_pct.plain_es: De cada 100 lugares turísticos del municipio, cuántos están a 400 m o menos de una parada registrada en el mapa, pero de ninguna parada con horario vigente. El horario de la parada terminó, o personas voluntarias registraron la parada y no existe un horario.
municipalities.acc_paper_pct.definition: The number of tourism places in the municipality that have a mapped stop of any kind within 400 m (transit_400m) but no stop with a current timetable within 400 m (ts_m above 400), divided by the tourism places counted (access_n), times 100, rounded to one decimal. Apart from rounding it equals transit_pct minus acc_cur400_pct. Such a place rests on a stop in a feed that has ended, or on a stop that volunteers mapped in OpenStreetMap with no timetable.
municipalities.acc_paper_pct.method: access.py counts the places with a mapped stop within 400 m and ts_m above 400 in each municipality and divides by the counted places.
municipalities.acc_paper_pct.how_to_read: A high value means that the figure for any mapped stop (transit_pct) overstates the access that a published timetable supports. In the 2026-10 snapshot the value is 15.4% island-wide (3,717 of 24,209 places; about 32% of the 11,507 places near any mapped stop). It ranges from 0.0 to 94.9 (Juncos), and 45 of the 78 municipalities have a value above 0. Five municipalities have 50% or more because their feed has ended: Juncos 94.9, Ponce 79.4, San Lorenzo 78.1, Fajardo 70.5 and Caguas 61.1. A high value is not proof that service stopped: a feed can run out of dates while buses still run.
caveats: Renewing a feed moves the places near its stops out of this share and into acc_cur400_pct.

Stops that volunteers mapped can be missing, out of date or wrong; the observatory does not check them on the ground. Where the operator publishes no feed at all, the nearby stops are only volunteer-mapped ones.
Públicos (shared taxis and vans), taxis, ride-hailing, rental cars and tour shuttles are in no timetable, so they are not counted.

Straight-line distance, not a walking route (see municipalities.walk_rule_400m). The share by walking along mapped roads is in the acc_walk fields (acc_walk400_pct, acc_walk800_pct, acc_wfreq400_pct).

municipalities.acc_cur800_pct.plain: Out of every 100 tourism places in the municipality, how many are within 800 m (half a mile), in a straight line, of a stop whose published timetable has not ended.
municipalities.acc_cur800_pct.plain_es: De cada 100 lugares turísticos del municipio, cuántos están a 800 m o menos (media milla), en línea recta, de una parada cuyo horario publicado no ha terminado.
municipalities.acc_cur800_pct.definition: The number of tourism places in the municipality whose distance to the nearest stop with a current timetable (ts_m in place_access.json) is 800 m or less, divided by the tourism places counted (access_n), times 100, rounded to one decimal. It includes the places within 400 m (acc_cur400_pct) and those 400 to 800 m away, which the map pop-up calls 'Stop 400–800 m away'.
municipalities.acc_cur800_pct.method: access.py counts the places with ts_m of 800 or less in each municipality and divides by the counted places. 800 m is a planning distance chosen for the observatory, not a measure of how far people walk.
municipalities.acc_cur800_pct.how_to_read: Use it to see how many more places a longer reach would add. In the 2026-10 snapshot the value is 36.2% island-wide (8,754 of 24,209 places), against 32.2% within 400 m, and ranges from 0.0 to 98.0 (San Juan). 43 of the 78 municipalities have 0.0. No map control shows this field; it is in municipalities.json and in the municipality table download.
caveats: Straight-line distance, not a walking route (see municipalities.walk_rule_400m). The share within an 800 m walk along mapped roads is acc_walk800_pct. 800 m is twice the 400 m used for most figures, and a straight line does not show whether the walk is safe or possible.

Públicos (shared taxis and vans), taxis, ride-hailing, rental cars and tour shuttles are in no timetable, so they are not counted.

place_access.tw_m.plain: How far a tourism place is from the nearest stop whose published timetable has not ended, walking along mapped roads. It is the distance behind the access class in the map pop-up. It is an estimate: the road map has no footpaths or sidewalks.
place_access.tw_m.plain_es: La distancia a pie, por las calles mapeadas, desde un lugar turístico hasta la parada más cercana cuyo horario publicado no ha terminado. Es la distancia detrás de la clase de acceso en la ventana del mapa. Es un estimado: el mapa de calles no tiene veredas ni aceras.
place_access.tw_m.definition: Meters walked from the place's map point to the nearest scheduled stop whose operator's timetable feed has an end date on or after the as-of date (as_of in place_access.json), along the roads of site/data/roads.bin except motorways and motorway links. A scheduled stop is a stop in the timetable feed (GTFS) of ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) or of a municipal transit system; ended feeds, volunteer-mapped stops, airports, taxi stands and chargers are not used. The distance is rounded up to whole meters, so a value of 400 or less is exactly the test behind the walking shares. The search stops at 1,000 m (walk_bound_m in the file): 99,999 means no such stop within a 1,000 m walk. A place with no walkable road within 150 m keeps its straight-line distance (ts_m) and is listed in tw_straight. The file has one value for each place of places.json, in the same order, joined by position like ts_m. On a place the map does not draw (see Counted but not drawn) the value is coarsened to one value per class: 400 (400 m or less), 800 (more than 400, up to 800), 1000 (more than 800, up to the 1,000 m bound) or 99,999 (beyond the bound); a place in tw_straight takes the coarsened ts_m; every count and share reads the same class as before (owner decision of 2026-10-18).
place_access.tw_m.method: walknet.py builds a walking network from site/data/roads.bin: every road except motorways and motorway links, usable in both directions. Each place and each stop with a current timetable is joined to the nearest walkable road within 150 m by a straight connector. access.py then searches the network from every such stop, up to 1,000 m (a bounded Dijkstra search), so the walking distance is connector + path along the roads + connector. Distances use the observatory's flat-earth formula on a plane centred on Puerto Rico, the same scale as ts_m. A walk is never shorter than the straight line, so tw_m is at least ts_m. Two cases fall back to the straight line so that nothing is silently dropped: a place with no walkable road within 150 m keeps its ts_m (it is listed in tw_straight), and a stop with no walkable road within 150 m (12 of 2,881 in the 2026-10 snapshot) counts at its straight-line distance.
place_access.tw_m.how_to_read: A smaller number means a shorter walk to a stop whose timetable is still in force. 400 or less is a stop within a 400 m walk; 401 to 800 is the 'Stop 400–800 m away' class of the pop-up; 99,999 means more than 1,000 m. Compare it with ts_m: the walk is a median 1.43 times the straight line where both are measured (90th percentile 2.43). In the 2026-10 snapshot 9,042 of the 32,541 places are within a 400 m walk, and so are 6,787 of the 24,209 places on the default basis (28.0%, against 32.2% in a straight line). 1,003 places on the default basis are within 400 m in a straight line but not on foot.
caveats: Along mapped roads, not every way a person can walk. The road file has no footways, paths, steps, pedestrian streets, sidewalks or crossings, and it does not know fences, gates or a road that is unsafe to cross. The visitor-access study (docs/analysis/visitor-access-2026-10) repeated the run on a full OpenStreetMap walking network: the island share within 400 m moved from 26.6% to 27.0%, and municipal shares moved a median 0.0 points (90th percentile 0.99, largest 11.3 in Hormigueros).

1,210 places (1,074 on the default basis, 4.4%) have no walkable road within 150 m and keep their straight-line distance (see place_access.tw_straight). For them the value is a lower bound: the real walk is at least that long.

Motorways and motorway links are left out because pedestrians cannot use them. A footbridge or underpass that the road file does not hold is missed, so a place across a motorway from a stop can read farther than it is.

Large grounds with no mapped public road inside (the airport, malls, resorts, campuses) make long detours. In the 2026-10 snapshot Carolina drops from 88.5% to 70.7% of places within 400 m, much of it around the airport and Plaza Carolina.
A stop with a current timetable is not proof of service. A timetable is a schedule: it does not show that vehicles run on time or at all. The observatory has no real-time data.
Públicos (shared taxis and vans), taxis, ride-hailing, rental cars and tour shuttles are in no timetable, so they are not counted.
The values change on the day a feed ends. In the 2026-10 snapshot 9 of the 18 current feeds end between 2026-10-31 and 2027-01-31, among them San Juan's municipal feed (see methods.access_profile).
Each distance starts at the place's listed point, which can be wrong in the source (Overture Maps).

Feed end dates: operators.json. Roads: OpenStreetMap (roads.py builds site/data/roads.bin from the Geofabrik extract; ODbL).

place_access.ts_calls.plain: The most scheduled calls on a typical weekday at any one stop with a current timetable within 400 m of the place. It is a rough sign of how often vehicles come. The app calls these calls weekday departures. 0 means there is no such stop within 400 m.
place_access.ts_calls.plain_es: La mayor cantidad de pasadas programadas en un día laborable típico en cualquier parada con horario vigente a 400 m o menos del lugar. Es una señal aproximada de con qué frecuencia pasan los vehículos. La aplicación llama a estas pasadas salidas en día laborable. Un 0 significa que no hay una parada así a 400 m o menos.
place_access.ts_calls.definition: For each place, the largest value of trips_weekday (see transit.stop_trips_weekday) among the scheduled stops within 400 m whose operator's feed has not ended on the as-of date, or 0 when there is none. trips_weekday is the number of calls (stop times) that the published timetable lists at the stop on a typical weekday (a Wednesday), counting every trip that calls there, whatever its direction. The app calls them weekday departures. A stop with 20 or more calls is a frequent stop in the observatory's access classes. 20 is a threshold chosen for the observatory, not a standard. On a place the map does not draw (see Counted but not drawn) the value is coarsened to 0 (none), 1 (1 to 19) or 20 (20 or more), the classes the access shares read (owner decision of 2026-10-18).
place_access.ts_calls.method: access.py takes the scheduled stops of operators whose feed has not ended that lie within 400 m of the place (straight line, same formula as ts_m) and keeps the largest trips_weekday. It is the largest single stop, not the sum of the stops.
place_access.ts_calls.how_to_read: A bigger number means a stop with more scheduled calls. In the 2026-10 snapshot 10,491 of the 32,541 places have a value above 0, the middle value among them is 30 and the largest is 508 (Terminal Covadonga). 5,163 of the 24,209 places on the default basis have 20 or more (21.3%). It is a proxy for frequency, not a headway (the time between vehicles): the calls are not spread evenly through the day, and a terminal's count includes vehicles that arrive there and end their run.
caveats: It counts calls in the timetable, not vehicles seen. The observatory has no real-time data.
It is the busiest single stop within 400 m, not a total. Two stops with 15 calls each give 15.
It describes a typical Wednesday. Holidays and other exceptions in the feeds are not applied (see transit.typical_weekday).
Only stops with a current timetable are read. A stop of an expired timetable can have more calls and is not counted.
In the 2026-10 snapshot ts_calls is 0 exactly for the places whose ts_m is above 400. In general a stop with no weekday call would also give 0, so read it with ts_m.
The ATI feed read on 2026-10-02 includes 30 trips of a holiday pattern that count as ordinary weekday service, so stops on ATI route 1 are slightly overstated (see transit.stop_trips_weekday).
Públicos (shared taxis and vans), taxis, ride-hailing, rental cars and tour shuttles are in no timetable, so they are not counted.

place_access.tw_calls.plain: The most scheduled calls on a typical weekday at any one stop with a current timetable within a 400 m walk of the place, along mapped roads. It is a rough sign of how often vehicles come. 0 means there is no such stop within a 400 m walk.
place_access.tw_calls.plain_es: La mayor cantidad de pasadas programadas en un día laborable típico en una sola parada con horario vigente a 400 m o menos a pie del lugar, por las calles mapeadas. Es una señal aproximada de cuán a menudo pasan los vehículos. 0 significa que no hay una parada así a 400 m o menos a pie.
place_access.tw_calls.definition: For each place, the largest value of trips_weekday (see transit.stop_trips_weekday) among the scheduled stops whose operator's feed has not ended on the as-of date and whose walking distance from the place (see tw_m) is 400 m or less, or 0 when there is none. It is ts_calls with the stops chosen by walking instead of a straight line. A place listed in tw_straight keeps its ts_calls. A stop with 20 or more calls is a frequent stop in the observatory's access classes; 20 is a threshold chosen for the observatory, not a standard. On a place the map does not draw (see Counted but not drawn) the value is coarsened to 0 (none), 1 (1 to 19) or 20 (20 or more), the classes the access shares read (owner decision of 2026-10-18).
place_access.tw_calls.method: access.py keeps, for each place, the walking distance to every stop with a current timetable reached within 1,000 m (see tw_m), and takes the largest trips_weekday among those within 400 m. It is the largest single stop, not the sum of the stops.
place_access.tw_calls.how_to_read: A bigger number means a stop with more scheduled calls within a short walk. In the 2026-10 snapshot 9,042 of the 32,541 places have a value above 0, the middle value among them is 26 and the largest is 508 (Terminal Covadonga). 4,366 of the 24,209 places on the default basis have 20 or more (18.0%, against 21.3% in a straight line). It is a proxy for frequency, not a headway.
caveats: It counts calls in the timetable, not vehicles seen. The observatory has no real-time data.
It is the busiest single stop within a 400 m walk, not a total. Two stops with 15 calls each give 15.
It describes a typical Wednesday. Holidays and other exceptions in the feeds are not applied (see transit.typical_weekday).

Along mapped roads, not every way a person can walk. The road file has no footways, paths, steps, pedestrian streets, sidewalks or crossings, and it does not know fences, gates or a road that is unsafe to cross. The visitor-access study (docs/analysis/visitor-access-2026-10) repeated the run on a full OpenStreetMap walking network: the island share within 400 m moved from 26.6% to 27.0%, and municipal shares moved a median 0.0 points (90th percentile 0.99, largest 11.3 in Hormigueros).
Públicos (shared taxis and vans), taxis, ride-hailing, rental cars and tour shuttles are in no timetable, so they are not counted.

place_access.ts_we.plain: Whether the published timetable gives Saturday service, Sunday service, both or neither at the stops with a current timetable within 400 m of the place. A 0 does not prove that there is no weekend service.
place_access.ts_we.plain_es: Si el horario publicado da servicio el sábado, el domingo, ambos días o ninguno en las paradas con horario vigente a 400 m o menos del lugar. Un 0 no prueba que no haya servicio de fin de semana.
place_access.ts_we.definition: A code made from two tests over the scheduled stops within 400 m whose operator's feed has not ended on the as-of date. Saturday: at least one of them has calls on a Saturday (calls_sat above 0 in transport.json), which adds 1. Sunday: at least one of them has calls on a Sunday (calls_sun above 0), which adds 2. The code is 0, 1, 2 or 3. The two tests can be met by different stops, so 3 does not mean that one stop has both.
place_access.ts_we.method: access.py reads calls_sat and calls_sun of the stops with a current timetable within 400 m. A stop with no Saturday call in the feed has no calls_sat field (see transit.stop_calls_sat).
place_access.ts_we.how_to_read: Use it with ts_m. A 0 beside a short ts_m means that the timetable shows weekday service only. It does not show that no vehicle runs on weekends. In the 2026-10 snapshot only 3 of the 18 current feeds list Saturday calls (ATI, Guaynabo and Vega Alta) and only ATI lists Sunday calls, so weekend service follows which feeds publish it. Of the 7,790 places on the default basis that are near a stop with a current timetable, 5,412 have Saturday service (69.5%) and 1,540 have Sunday service (19.8%).
caveats: Missing is not zero. A feed with no weekend calls may leave out weekend service, or the service may run without a published timetable.

It is a typical Saturday and a typical Sunday. Holidays and other exceptions in the feeds are not applied, and the dates when a service pattern starts and ends are not checked (see transit.typical_weekday).
It does not say how often vehicles come at the weekend. The calls at each stop are in calls_sat and calls_sun of transport.json.
A stop with a current timetable is not proof of service. A timetable is a schedule: it does not show that vehicles run on time or at all. The observatory has no real-time data.
Públicos (shared taxis and vans), taxis, ride-hailing, rental cars and tour shuttles are in no timetable, so they are not counted.

values.0: Neither Saturday nor Sunday service in the published timetable at a stop with a current timetable within 400 m, or no such stop within 400 m. 27,248 places in the 2026-10 snapshot: 23,836 with no such stop within 400 m and 3,412 whose stops list weekday service only.
values.1: Saturday service and no Sunday service. 5,821 places in the 2026-10 snapshot.
values.2: Sunday service and no Saturday service. 0 places in the 2026-10 snapshot: every stop with Sunday calls also has Saturday calls.
values.3: Saturday and Sunday service. 2,049 places in the 2026-10 snapshot.

places.transit_400m.plain: Yes when a mapped stop, station or terminal of any kind is 400 m (a quarter mile) or less from the place, including stops whose timetable has ended and stops that volunteers mapped. The field is missing when the nearest stop is farther.
places.transit_400m.plain_es: Sí cuando hay una parada, estación o terminal de cualquier tipo del mapa a 400 m (un cuarto de milla) o menos del lugar, incluidas las paradas cuyo horario terminó y las que mapearon personas voluntarias. El campo no aparece cuando la parada más cercana está más lejos.
places.transit_400m.definition: A yes flag (true). In the 2026-10 snapshot, it is present for 15,588 of 32,541 places (47.9%) and for 11,507 of 24,209 places on the default basis (47.5%).
places.transit_400m.method: True when the straight-line distance to the nearest stop of any kind is 400 m or less. The distance is tested before it is cut to whole meters. The municipal share transit_pct counts this flag on the default basis.
places.transit_400m.how_to_read: It is a supply-side sign of car-free access to a stop, not to service: it counts stops whose timetable has ended and stops that volunteers mapped. For a stop with a current timetable, use ts_m of 400 or less in place_access.json. It does not account for how often vehicles run, the hours, or whether the walk is safe. Default basis means a confidence score of 0.50 or higher and no places of worship. Earlier versions of the observatory labelled the field 'within 400 m of transit'.
caveats: In the 2026-10 access update the flag was recomputed from today's stop list. 130 places gained it and none lost it; 129 of the 130 are in Jayuya, whose stops had a wrong longitude before. See municipalities.transit_data_updates.
The distance is cut to whole meters after the test, so a place at 400.6 m shows 400 and has no flag. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 14 places in the file (11 on the default basis) are in this case.

Stops with expired timetables and OpenStreetMap stops with no timetable still count. In the 2026-10 snapshot 3,717 of the 11,507 default-basis places with the flag have no stop with a current timetable within 400 m (see municipalities.acc_paper_pct).

The stop list mixes sources with different terms: the ATI feed (provided as is, with no warranty), municipal GTFS feeds (no license stated) and OpenStreetMap (Open Database License, ODbL; credit OpenStreetMap contributors). Check each source's terms before you reuse stop names or distances.
The place counts in the table of codes are from the 2026-10 snapshot.

values.true: A mapped stop of any kind is 400 m or less from the pin. 15,588 places.
values.(missing): The nearest mapped stop is more than 400 m from the pin. The field is left out of the file instead of being written as false.

municipalities.place_bases.plain: Two place counts are in use. Transit shares count tourism places. Land use plan shares of places count every place listing. This entry sets them side by side.
municipalities.place_bases.plain_es: Se usan dos conteos de lugares. Las proporciones de transporte colectivo cuentan lugares turísticos. Las proporciones de lugares según el plan de uso de terrenos cuentan todos los registros de lugares. Esta entrada los pone lado a lado.
municipalities.place_bases.definition: Tourism places (field assets; used by transit_pct, places_near_transit and the acc_ shares, with access_n as the number counted): Overture Maps places that Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR) classified into the observatory's categories and de-duplicated, with confidence 0.50 or higher and places of worship left out. All listings (used by places_on_protected_land, places_on_protected_land_pct and places_urban_pct): the same places with no confidence cut-off and with places of worship. In both cases a place belongs to the municipality where its point falls, not to the municipality in its address.
municipalities.place_bases.method: build.py sets the municipality from each place's point and computes assets with the filter above. landuse.py receives the whole place list, without the filter, so its place counts and shares use all listings.
municipalities.place_bases.how_to_read: Do not compare places_on_protected_land with assets or with in_protected directly: they count different sets of places. In the 2026-10 snapshot the island has 24,209 tourism places and 32,541 listings: the listings are the 24,209 tourism places plus 3,300 below confidence 0.50 and 5,032 places of worship.
caveats: The other place counts in municipalities.json (assets, in_sfha, in_protected, with_website, places_near_transit, access_n and the acc_ shares) use the tourism places basis; the three land use place fields are the exception.
The map's filters (confidence, categories, places of worship) change the places on screen, not these stored fields.
municipalities.place_bases.source_detail: Overture Maps places; build.py (MIN_CONF = 0.50) and landuse.py
